+`bobtrace` is a Python package that lets a developer point at any directory of Python source files, automatically inject a `@bob_trace` decorator onto every function via AST rewriting, and then read back structured execution evidence through an MCP server that Bob (or any agent) calls to diagnose bugs, explain latency, and generate regression tests — without the developer having to add a single line of instrumentation manually.
+
+**Scope**
+
+| Layer | What it does |
+|---|---|
+| `bobtrace/tracer.py` | Runtime: `@bob_trace` decorator, context propagation via `ContextVar`, span recording, JSONL flush |
+| `bobtrace/injector.py` | AST-based injector/ejector: rewrites source files to add/remove the decorator and import |
+| `bobtrace/store.py` | Pure analysis functions shared by the MCP server and the CLI |
+| `bobtrace/mcp_server.py` | Stdio MCP server: 7 tools the agent calls |
+| `bobtrace/cli.py` / `main.py` | Entry point: `inject`, `eject`, `diagnose`, `latency`, `report`, `failures`, `gen-test` subcommands |
+| `.bob/` | `mcp.json.example`, `custom_modes.yaml`, and three skills |
+| `tests/` | Unit and integration tests for each layer |
+| `sandbox/` | A small FastAPI app used for demo/integration testing — bugs are intentional and undocumented in the repo |
+
+**Non-goals**
+
+- No middleware injection; no special FastAPI handling.
+- No log forwarding, metrics export, or OpenTelemetry compatibility.
+- No per-request files, no rotation — one append-only `traces/traces.jsonl`.
+- No distributed tracing across process boundaries.
+
+---
+
+## Sub-Tasks
+
+---
+
+### Sub-Task 1 — Package skeleton and project files
+
+**Intent**
+Establish the installable package layout, dependencies, and entry points so every subsequent sub-task has a stable home.
+
+**Expected Outcomes**
+
+- `pyproject.toml` defines the `bobtrace` package and a `bobtrace` CLI entry point.
+- Core package (`bobtrace/`) has **no third-party dependencies** — standard library only.
+- `mcp` is an optional server extra; `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `pytest`, and `httpx` are demo/test extras.
+- Running `pip install -e ".[server,dev]"` succeeds.
+- `.bob/mcp.json.example` skeleton exists; `.bob/mcp.json` is gitignored.
+- `tests/__init__.py` and `tests/generated/.gitkeep` exist.
+
+**Dependency groups in `pyproject.toml`**
+
+```
+[project]           # no dependencies
+[project.optional-dependencies]
+server = ["mcp"]
+dev    = ["fastapi", "uvicorn", "httpx", "pytest"]
+```
+
+**Todo List**
+
+1. Create `bobtrace/__init__.py` (version string only).
+2. Create `pyproject.toml` with the dependency groups above and `[project.scripts]` entry `bobtrace = bobtrace.cli:main`.
+3. Create `main.py` thin shim calling `bobtrace.cli:main`.
+4. Create `tests/__init__.py` and `tests/generated/.gitkeep`.
+5. Create `.bob/mcp.json.example` skeleton (interpreter path left as `"<venv>/Scripts/python.exe"` on Windows, `"<venv>/bin/python"` on Unix).
+6. Add `.bob/mcp.json` to `.gitignore`.
+7. Create `sandbox/` directory with a `__init__.py` and placeholder files (`app.py`, `models.py`, `db.py`) — actual bug content is written by the implementer without documenting the bugs.
+
+**Relevant Context**
+
+- `sandbox/README.md` must NOT describe the intentional bugs. Its existence would let an agent skip diagnosis entirely.
+- `.bob/mcp.json` uses the absolute path to the venv interpreter. On Windows: `...\.venv\Scripts\python.exe`. A venv built inside WSL will not start from a Windows Bob.
+
+**Status** `[ ] pending`
+
+---
+
+### Sub-Task 2 — Runtime tracer (`bobtrace/tracer.py`)
+
+**Intent**
+Implement the `@bob_trace` decorator and everything needed to record spans, propagate context, and flush complete traces to JSONL — with no third-party dependencies.
+
+**Expected Outcomes**
+
+- `from bobtrace.tracer import bob_trace` works with stdlib only.
+- A decorated call with nothing in the `ContextVar` creates a new `trace_id`, a new buffer, and becomes the root span.
+- A decorated call that finds a buffer in the `ContextVar` joins the same `trace_id` as a child.
+- The full trace is flushed as **one `write()` call per trace** (all spans, each on its own line, concatenated) when the root span finishes. One atomic write prevents concurrent processes from interleaving lines.
+- Error traces are always written. Successful traces are sampled at `BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE` (float 0–1, default `1.0`).
+- A single trace is capped at 500 spans; the root span carries `dropped_spans` when the cap is hit.
+- `BOBTRACE_FILE` overrides the output path; an empty string disables file output.
+- Works for both sync and async functions.
+- `BaseException` (but not `Exception`) closes the span as `cancelled` and is re-raised immediately.
+- `Exception` closes the span as `error` and is re-raised unchanged.
+- Failures inside the tracer itself are swallowed so they never affect the application.
+
+**ContextVar value structure**
+
+The `ContextVar` holds a single value: a named triple `(trace_id, current_span_id, buffer)`. The buffer is an object with three attributes: `spans` (list), `has_error` (bool), `dropped` (int). A new root call creates the buffer; all children inherit it through the same `ContextVar` value. There is no module-level span list.
+
+**Raw span schema (written to JSONL — one span per line)**
+
+| Field | Always present | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| `trace_id` | yes | UUID |
+| `span_id` | yes | UUID |
+| `parent_span_id` | yes | UUID or `null` for root |
+| `function_name` | yes | Simple name (`__name__`) |
+| `module` | yes | `__module__` of the function |
+| `qualname` | yes | `__qualname__` |
+| `source_file` | yes | Absolute path (made project-relative in the read path) |
+| `source_line` | yes | Line number of the `def` |
+| `start_time` | yes | ISO-8601 UTC |
+| `status` | yes | `success`, `error`, or `cancelled` |
+| `execution_time_ms` | yes | Wall time of this span |
+| `inputs` | yes | Serialised argument dict (see serialisation spec) |
+| `response` | on success | Serialised return value |
+| `error_type` | on error | Exception class name |
+| `error_message` | on error | `"<Type>: <str(exc)>"` — used as the bug title |
+| `error_location` | on error | `"file:line"` of the raise site (innermost traceback frame) |
+| `dropped_spans` | root only | Integer, only present when cap was hit |
+
+**Input serialisation spec**
+
+- Bind arguments to parameter names using the signature cached at decoration time (`inspect.signature`).
+- Serialise without running arbitrary user code: JSON scalars and stdlib containers pass through as-is (max depth 6, max 50 items per container, max 2 000-char strings).
+- `Pydantic` models: call `.model_dump()` if available.
+- `datetime`, `Decimal`, `UUID`, `Path`, `Enum`, `bytes`: `repr()`.
+- Everything else: `__dict__` or `__slots__` plus a `__type__` key.
+- Redact fields whose name matches `password`, `token`, `email`, `phone`, or any key in `BOBTRACE_REDACT_KEYS` (comma-separated env var) to `"***REDACTED***"`. Redacted inputs are **recorded and written** — they do not prevent span recording or test generation.
+- A re-entrancy guard: if the tracer's own serialisation code calls a traced function, that inner call records nothing.
+
+**Todo List**
+
+1. Define the `Span` dataclass with all fields listed in the schema above.
+2. Define the `TraceBuffer` dataclass: `spans`, `has_error`, `dropped`.
+3. Implement the `ContextVar[Optional[Tuple[str, str, TraceBuffer]]]` with helpers to read/set the current context.
+4. Implement `bob_trace` as a decorator factory wrapping both sync and async callables: create buffer on root entry, link parent on child entry, record span on exit, flush on root exit.
+5. Implement the input serialisation function with depth/size limits, type dispatch, redaction, and re-entrancy guard.
+6. Implement the flush function: serialize each span to a JSON string, concatenate with newlines, write the whole string in a single `file.write()` call.
+7. Implement sampling and the 500-span cap with `dropped_spans` on the root span.
+8. Write unit tests in `tests/test_tracer.py`: root span creation, child linking, error fields, `BaseException` → `cancelled`, async support, sampling, span cap, serialisation depth/redaction/re-entrancy, single-write flush (mock `open` and assert one `write` call per trace).
+
+**Relevant Context**
+
+- `self_ms` is a **read-path concern** computed in `store.py`, not written by the tracer.
+- `module` and `qualname` are needed by `generate_regression_test` to import and call the function.
+- `source_file` is stored absolute by the tracer; `store.py` makes it project-relative in all agent-facing payloads.
+
+**Status** `[ ] pending`
+
+---
+
+### Sub-Task 3 — AST injector/ejector (`bobtrace/injector.py`)
+
+**Intent**
+Implement the source-rewriting engine that adds and removes `@bob_trace` decorators and the matching import, fully reversibly and idempotently, with atomic file writes.
+
+**Expected Outcomes**
+
+- `inject_file` adds `@bob_trace` immediately above every `def` / `async def` that does not already have it, and adds the import line.
+- Per-function idempotency: a function that already has `@bob_trace` is skipped; other functions in the same file are still processed.
+- `eject_file` removes lines that are exactly `@bob_trace` (with any leading indent matching the `def`) and the exact import line; resulting bytes match the pre-inject file.
+- Both operations `compile()` the result before writing; if compilation fails the original file is left untouched.
+- Files are written atomically (write to a temp file, then `os.replace`).
+- CRLF line endings are preserved end-to-end.
+- `--dry-run` prints a unified diff and exits 0 without writing.
+
+**Skip rules (per function)**
+
+- Already has `@bob_trace` on the line immediately above → skip silently.
+- Is a dunder method other than `__init__` or `__call__` → skip silently.
+- Body contains a call to `sys._getframe`, `inspect.currentframe`, `inspect.stack`, or the same family → skip and **report** with reason.
+- File's absolute path is inside the `bobtrace` package → refuse entire file with an error.
+
+**Do NOT skip** `__init__.py` or files under `tests/`.
+
+**Import placement**
+
+Insert `from bobtrace.tracer import bob_trace` after the module docstring and any `__future__` imports, before anything else. Eject removes that exact line. No sentinel comment.
+
+**Trade-off to document:** a pre-existing manual `from bobtrace.tracer import bob_trace` will be removed by eject. Acceptable; document in the README.
+
+**Todo List**
+
+1. Implement `inject_file(path, dry_run)` using the `ast` module to locate `FunctionDef`/`AsyncFunctionDef` line numbers; perform line-level text insertion (not `ast.unparse`) to preserve formatting and comments.
+2. Apply per-function skip logic (existing decorator, dunder filter, frame-inspection detection, bobtrace-package guard).
+3. Implement `eject_file(path, dry_run)`: remove `@bob_trace` decorator lines and the exact import line.
+4. Add `compile()` validation and atomic `os.replace` write.
+5. Detect and preserve CRLF.
+6. Implement `inject` and `eject` CLI subcommands in `bobtrace/cli.py` that walk the target directory, call the per-file function, and print a summary line.
+7. Add `--dry-run` unified diff output using `difflib.unified_diff`.
+8. Write unit tests in `tests/test_injector.py`: inject → eject produces original bytes, double-inject is idempotent per-function, dry-run writes nothing, dunders skipped (except `__init__`/`__call__`), frame-inspection functions reported, CRLF round-trips, bobtrace files refused.
+
+**Relevant Context**
+
+- `@bob_trace` sits on the line immediately above `def`/`async def`, inside any existing decorators (e.g. `@app.get` stays above `@bob_trace`).
+- No sentinel comment — eject identifies injected lines by their exact text.
+
+**Status** `[ ] pending`
+
+---
+
+### Sub-Task 4 — Analysis store (`bobtrace/store.py`) and MCP server (`bobtrace/mcp_server.py`)
+
+**Intent**
+Implement all 7 analysis functions as pure Python in `store.py`, wire exactly 7 of them as MCP tools in `mcp_server.py`, and update `.bob/mcp.json.example`. `load_traces` and `compute_self_ms` are internal helpers, not MCP tools.
+
+**MCP SDK compatibility note**
+
+Try `from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer` first; fall back to `from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP`. Insert the project root into `sys.path[0]` at module top so `sandbox.app` (and any other target package) is importable regardless of the directory the client launched from.
+
+**Read-path computed fields** (derived in `store.py`, never written by the tracer)
+
+- `self_ms`: span's `execution_time_ms` minus the sum of its direct children's `execution_time_ms`.
+- Propagation label: an error span whose direct child also has `status == error` gets `error: "propagated <Type> from child"` in compact views; raw `error_type`/`error_message`/`error_location` are still used for grouping.
+- All file paths in agent-facing payloads are **project-relative** (strip the project root prefix). Absolute paths waste tokens and leak local directories.
+
+**Analysis functions and MCP tools (7 tools registered)**
+
+| Tool | CLI cmd | Key inputs | Key outputs |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `diagnose` | `diagnose` | _(none)_ | Root-cause groups — START HERE for errors |
+| `explain_latency` | `latency` | `trace_id` (optional) | `self_time_by_function`, `hot_path`, `n_plus_one_suspects`, `caveats` — START HERE for slowness |
+| `generate_regression_test` | `gen-test` | `span_id`, `write` (bool default `true`) | `path`+`source` or `filename`+`source` |
+| `get_trace` | _(MCP only)_ | `trace_id` | Compact nested tree |
+| `list_failures` | `failures` | `limit` (int default 10) | Root-cause groups, ≤ 3 example span IDs each |
+| `trace_summary` | `report` | _(none)_ | Per-function stats, errors first |
+| `get_slowest` | _(MCP only)_ | `limit` (int default 10) | Slowest spans by `execution_time_ms`, each with `self_ms` |
+
+**`diagnose` / `list_failures` root-cause spec**
+
+A distinct bug is an error span with **no failing child** (the deepest error in the chain), grouped by `(function_name, error_type, error_location)`. Each group:
+
+- `occurrences`: count of matching spans
+- `affected_entry_points`: distinct `function_name` of root spans containing this bug
+- `location`: project-relative `source_file:error_location` (the **raise** line, not the `def` line)
+- `source_snippet`: up to 5 lines from disk centred on the raise line; failing line prefixed with `>> ` and line numbers shown; wrapped in try/except so missing files don't crash the tool
+- `call_path`: ordered list of `{fn, inputs}` from root span to error span
+- `example_span_ids`: up to 3 span IDs
+- `next_step`: always `"generate_regression_test(span_id='<example_span_id>')"` — no heuristic
+
+**`explain_latency` spec**
+
+With no `trace_id`: scan all spans where `parent_span_id == null`, pick the one with the highest `execution_time_ms`. If none, return `{"error": "no traces recorded"}`.
+With a `trace_id`: analyse all spans sharing that ID.
+
+Output:
+- `self_time_by_function`: list of `{fn, call_count, self_ms, share_pct}` sorted by `self_ms` desc
+- `hot_path`: greedy walk from root — at each node descend into the child with the largest `execution_time_ms`; stop at a leaf; returns list of `{fn, span_id, ms}`
+- `n_plus_one_suspects`: see N+1 spec below
+- `caveats`: trust-the-numbers warnings only — e.g. `"Root span ended with status=error; timings stop at the failure"` and `"Fewer than 5 recorded requests for this entry point; confirm with more traffic"`. Not span-drop counts.
+
+**N+1 detection spec**
+
+Within one trace a parent is a suspect when it calls the same child `function_name` ≥ 3 times AND those calls are **sequential** (each call's `start_time ≥ previous start_time + execution_time_ms − 0.1 ms`). Parallel calls of the same child are not a suspect.
+
+Report per suspect: `parent_fn`, `child_fn`, `call_count`, `total_ms`, `pct_of_request`, `heaviest_inner_fn` (the `function_name` with the most total `self_ms` among descendants of those calls).
+
+**`get_trace` compact node spec**
+
+Each node: `fn`, `span_id`, `status`, `ms` (`execution_time_ms`), `self_ms`, `inputs`. On success: `response`. On error: `error` (`"propagated <Type> from child"` if a direct child also failed, otherwise `error_message`), `at` (project-relative `error_location`, only on the originating span). Children in `calls` ordered by `start_time`.
+
+**`generate_regression_test` spec**
+
+- Takes `span_id` (required). Does not fall back to latest failure.
+- Requires `module` and `qualname` on the span.
+- Refuse with an error string if: `qualname` contains `<locals>` (nested function) OR `qualname` contains `.` and does not end in `.__init__` or `.__call__` (method). These two checks are distinct.
+- Spans with redacted inputs (`"***REDACTED***"`) are **not refused**: generate the test and add a header comment `# NOTE: replace ***REDACTED*** values with safe fixture values before running`.
+- Filename: `tests/generated/test_replay_<qualname>_<span_id[:8]>.py` (sanitise qualname for filesystem).
+- Generated test file sets `os.environ["BOBTRACE_FILE"] = ""` and `os.environ["BOBTRACE_CONSOLE"] = "off"` before importing the target, so running the test suite does not record traces of itself.
+- **Error span** → test that **fails while the bug still exists**:
+  ```python
+  # The test should FAIL until the bug is fixed.
+  result = function(**inputs)
+  # if recorded exception type is still raised → pytest.fail("still raises <Type>")
+  # if a different exception is raised → re-raise it (let pytest report it)
+  # if the call returns without error → pytest.fail("Bug no longer reproduces. Replace this line with an assertion on the intended result.")
+  ```
+- **Success span** → characterization test: `assert serialize(result) == RECORDED_RESPONSE`.
+- `write=True` (default): write file, return `{"path": ..., "source": ...}`.
+- `write=False`: return `{"filename": ..., "source": ...}` only.
+
+**Todo List**
+
+1. Implement `load_traces(path)` — reads JSONL, returns a flat list of span dicts and a dict `{trace_id: [spans]}`.
+2. Implement `compute_self_ms(spans)` — for each span, subtract direct children's `execution_time_ms`.
+3. Implement `diagnose(traces)` with root-cause grouping, `source_snippet` with `>> ` marker, project-relative paths, and fixed `next_step`.
+4. Implement `explain_latency(traces, trace_id=None)` with `self_time_by_function`, greedy `hot_path`, N+1 detection, and trust-the-numbers `caveats`.
+5. Implement `list_failures(traces, limit=10)`.
+6. Implement `trace_summary(traces)` — errors first.
+7. Implement `get_slowest(traces, limit=10)` — by `execution_time_ms`, include `self_ms`, project-relative paths.
+8. Implement `get_trace(traces, trace_id)` — compact nested tree with propagation labels.
+9. Implement `generate_regression_test(traces, span_id, write=True)` with all validation, redaction note, env-var header, and both test templates.
+10. Wire the 7 MCP tools in `mcp_server.py` with MCPServer/FastMCP fallback, `sys.path` insertion, and docstrings containing "START HERE for errors" / "START HERE for slowness" on the appropriate tools.
+11. Update `.bob/mcp.json.example` with the correct command using the venv interpreter path placeholder.
+12. Write unit tests in `tests/test_store.py` for each function using fixture JSONL data covering: root-cause grouping, N+1 detection, hot-path walk, regression test templates, redacted-input note, nested/method refusal.
+
+**Status** `[ ] pending`
+
+---
+
+### Sub-Task 5 — CLI entry point (`bobtrace/cli.py` and `main.py`)
+
+**Intent**
+Wire all subcommands into a single `argparse`-based CLI. Analysis subcommands call `store.py` directly — the same functions the MCP server calls.
+
+**Expected Outcomes**
+
+- `bobtrace inject --target <dir> [--dry-run]` works.
+- `bobtrace eject --target <dir> [--dry-run]` works.
+- `bobtrace diagnose` prints root-cause groups as JSON.
+- `bobtrace latency [--trace-id <id>]` prints the latency report as JSON.
+- `bobtrace report` prints `trace_summary` as JSON.
+- `bobtrace failures [--limit N]` prints `list_failures` as JSON.
+- `bobtrace gen-test --span-id <id> [--no-write]` generates a regression test.
+- Exit code 0 on success, non-zero on error.
+- All analysis commands respect `BOBTRACE_FILE` for the trace path.
+
+**Todo List**
+
+1. Implement `cli.py` with `argparse` subcommands: `inject`, `eject`, `diagnose`, `latency`, `report`, `failures`, `gen-test`.
+2. `main.py` calls `bobtrace.cli:main`.
+3. Analysis subcommands call `load_traces` then the appropriate `store.py` function and pretty-print as JSON.
+4. Add `--help` text to every argument.
+5. Write a smoke test in `tests/test_cli.py`: inject/eject against a temp dir; diagnose/latency against a fixture JSONL.
+
+**Status** `[ ] pending`
+
+---
+
+### Sub-Task 6 — Bob layer (`.bob/` config)
+
+**Intent**
+Give Bob the mode, skills, and MCP registration it needs to call `diagnose` before guessing, write a failing test before editing, and never touch `bobtrace/` itself.
+
+**Expected Outcomes**
+
+- `.bob/custom_modes.yaml` defines a `bobtrace-debugger` mode.
+- Three skill files exist in `.bob/skills/`: `trace-to-fix.md`, `explain-slowness.md`, `instrument-codebase.md`.
+- `.bob/mcp.json.example` (from Sub-Task 1) is updated with the correct command.
+- A developer can activate the mode and follow the workflow without extra prompting.
+
+**`bobtrace-debugger` mode constraints**
+
+- Call `diagnose` or `explain_latency` before reading any source file.
+- Generate a failing regression test (via `generate_regression_test`) before making any code edit.
+- Ask the user when intended behavior is a product decision, not an engineering fact.
+- Make the minimal fix that gets the generated test to pass.
+- Never edit files inside `bobtrace/` or remove `@bob_trace` decorators.
+
+**Skill outlines**
+
+| Skill | Trigger | Steps |
+|---|---|---|
+| `trace-to-fix` | A service is failing or throwing errors | Call `diagnose` → pick the top group → call `generate_regression_test` → reproduce locally → fix → confirm test passes |
+| `explain-slowness` | A service is slow or timing out | Call `explain_latency` → read `n_plus_one_suspects` and `hot_path` → form a hypothesis → call `get_trace` on the slowest trace → fix → re-run |
+| `instrument-codebase` | A service has no tracing | Run `bobtrace inject --target <dir>` → confirm inject summary → run the app → trigger failing paths → call `diagnose` |
+
+**Todo List**
+
+1. Write `.bob/custom_modes.yaml` with the `bobtrace-debugger` mode definition, role description, and constraints.
+2. Write `.bob/skills/trace-to-fix.md`.
+3. Write `.bob/skills/explain-slowness.md`.
+4. Write `.bob/skills/instrument-codebase.md`.
+5. Verify `.bob/mcp.json.example` references `python -m bobtrace.mcp_server` with the interpreter placeholder.
+
+**Status** `[ ] pending`
+
+---
+
+### Sub-Task 7 — Sandbox app and integration tests
+
+**Intent**
+Provide a realistic demo target and prove the full loop works end-to-end. The sandbox bugs are intentional but **not documented in any repo file** — the agent must discover them through tracing.
+
+**Expected Outcomes**

+- `sandbox/app.py` is a working FastAPI app with at least one buggy endpoint and one N+1 endpoint. It has no bobtrace references before injection.
+- Running `inject → start app → hit endpoints → stop app` produces a `traces/traces.jsonl` with at least one error trace and one slow trace.
+- `tests/test_integration.py` exercises inject → call a traced function → eject → verify source restored (bytes match).
+- `README.md` has a Quick Start section with exact commands.
+- `sandbox/README.md` describes what the app does but says nothing about where the bugs are.
+
+**Todo List**
+
+1. Write `sandbox/app.py`, `sandbox/models.py`, `sandbox/db.py` with intentional but undocumented bugs.
+2. Write `sandbox/README.md` (describes the app's purpose, endpoints, and how to start it — no bug hints).
+3. Write `tests/test_integration.py`.
+4. Write `README.md` with Quick Start, Bob MCP setup, example Bob prompts for each tool, and the eject trade-off note.
+
+**Relevant Context**
+
+- The integration test calls Python functions directly; no running HTTP server is required.
+- `sandbox/README.md` must not describe the intentional bugs — this is the answer key the demo depends on.
+
+**Status** `[ ] pending`
+

+

|---|---|---|
| 1 | Flush wrote one line per trace | Flush now serialises each span to its own line, concatenates them, and calls a **single** `file.write()` per trace |
| 2 | Span buffer was module-level | `ContextVar` now holds a triple `(trace_id, span_id, buffer)`; `buffer` carries `spans`, `has_error`, `dropped`; children inherit the same buffer object |
| 3 | Redacted inputs refused test generation | Redacted inputs are **recorded and written**; the generated test gets a header comment telling the agent to replace `***REDACTED***` with fixture values |
| 4 | Nested vs method refusal conflated | Two distinct checks: `<locals>` in qualname = nested function; `.` in qualname that is not `__init__`/`__call__` = method |
| 5 | `next_step` had a latency heuristic | Always emits `"generate_regression_test(span_id='<id>')"` — no branching |
| 6 | `hot_path` used cumulative self_ms | Hot path is now a greedy walk: at each node descend into the child with the largest `execution_time_ms` |
| 7 | `diagnose` location was the `def` line | Location is `error_location` (the raise line); snippet centred there with `>> ` marker and line numbers |
| 8 | Paths were absolute in payloads | All agent-facing payloads use project-relative paths |
| 9 | `caveats` included span-drop counts | Caveats are trust-the-numbers warnings only (root ended in error, fewer than 5 requests) |
| 10 | `error_message` was `str(exc)` | Now `"<Type>: <str(exc)>"` for use as a bug title |
| 11 | MCP SDK import was fragile | Try `MCPServer` first, fall back to `FastMCP`; `sys.path` insertion at module top |
| 12 | `.bob/mcp.json` used `python` | Uses venv absolute path placeholder; file is gitignored; `.example` is committed |
| 13 | Generated tests recorded traces | Tests set `BOBTRACE_FILE=""` and `BOBTRACE_CONSOLE=off` before importing the target |
| 14 | `sandbox/README.md` had bug hints | Describes the app only — no bug locations. The bugs are the answer key |
| 15 | No Bob layer sub-task | Added **Sub-Task 6**: `bobtrace-debugger` mode, three skills (`trace-to-fix`, `explain-slowness`, `instrument-codebase`) |
| 16 | Wrong dependency groups | Core = stdlib only; `mcp` = server extra; `fastapi`/`uvicorn`/`pytest`/`httpx` = dev extra |

---

## Architecture at a glance

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Developer: python main.py inject --target ./sandbox] --> B[bobtrace/injector.py]
    B --> C[sandbox/*.py: @bob_trace on every function]
    C --> D[App runs: traces/traces.jsonl]
    D --> E[bobtrace/store.py: 7 analysis functions]
    E --> F[bobtrace/mcp_server.py: stdio MCP]
    E --> G[bobtrace/cli.py: diagnose / latency / report / failures / gen-test]
    F --> H[Bob in bobtrace-debugger mode]
    H -->|calls diagnose - START HERE for errors| E
    H -->|calls explain_latency - START HERE for slowness| E
    H -->|calls generate_regression_test| I[tests/generated/test_replay_*.py]
    I --> J[pytest: test fails while bug exists]
    H --> K[Minimal code fix]
    K --> J
    J -->|passes| L[Bug proven fixed]
```

---

## Validation questions before you approve

1. **Sub-Task 6 (Bob layer)** — should the three skills be full step-by-step instruction documents, or concise trigger+checklist files? And should `bobtrace-debugger` be a standalone mode or extend an existing mode (e.g. agent)?
2. **`get_trace` compact tree** — the plan caps redacted values at display time. Should `inputs` in the compact tree also show `***REDACTED***`, or strip those keys entirely?
3. **`trace_summary` p50/p95** — computed across all recorded spans for that function, including dropped traces. Is that acceptable, or should only complete (non-dropped) traces contribute to percentiles?
4. Does the 7-sub-task order and the dependency graph match how you want to build this?

Answers, then go build.

Skills: concise, but numbered and ordered, not a bare checklist. Frontmatter with name and description, then roughly 30 to 45 lines of numbered steps. trace-to-fix needs two things a checklist would lose: an explicit "do not skip the reproduce step," and a default decision policy for when the user asked for unattended work (neutral value when the input is legal for the API, a deliberate validation error the framework turns into 4xx when the input is invalid for the business). Without that policy an unattended agent stalls at the product question. The other two skills can be shorter.

Standalone mode. Give it slug, name, description, whenToUse, roleDefinition, customInstructions, and groups: [read, edit, execute, mcp, skill]. The whole point is the constraints, and inheriting a general agent mode dilutes them. One line to add to customInstructions that is not in your plan: never paste a ***REDACTED*** value into code or tests.

Show ***REDACTED***, do not strip the key. A missing key reads as "this argument was not passed," which sends the agent down a wrong path. The marker tells it a value existed and is deliberately hidden, which is also what the generated test needs to warn about.

Percentiles over everything in the file is correct, and the dropped-trace concern does not exist. Spans past the 500 cap are never written, so they cannot contribute. The real bias is sampling: successful traces are sampled while error traces are always kept, so at a sample rate below 1 the error rate in trace_summary is inflated. Worth one caveat line in that output when the sample rate is not 1. Do not try to exclude anything.

One change to the order: move sandbox/ to the front, before sub-task 1, and write it yourself. Everything else stands. As drawn, the app you demo against is authored in sub-task 7 by the same agent that then diagnoses it, and the integration test in that sub-task has nothing to run against until the very end. Build it by hand first, commit it undecorated, and sub-task 4 gets a real target to check diagnose against instead of only fixture JSONL.

arguments.content:
# bobtrace — Plan

## Top-Level Overview

`bobtrace` is a Python package that lets a developer point at any directory of Python source files, automatically inject a `@bob_trace` decorator onto every function via AST rewriting, and then read back structured execution evidence through an MCP server that Bob (or any agent) calls to diagnose bugs, explain latency, and generate regression tests — without the developer having to add a single line of instrumentation manually.

**Scope**

| Layer | What it does |
|---|---|
| `sandbox/` | Demo FastAPI app — written by hand before any other sub-task, committed undecorated |
| `bobtrace/tracer.py` | Runtime: `@bob_trace` decorator, context propagation via `ContextVar`, span recording, JSONL flush |
| `bobtrace/injector.py` | AST-based injector/ejector: rewrites source files to add/remove the decorator and import |
| `bobtrace/store.py` | Pure analysis functions shared by the MCP server and the CLI |
| `bobtrace/mcp_server.py` | Stdio MCP server: 7 tools the agent calls |
| `bobtrace/cli.py` / `main.py` | Entry point: `inject`, `eject`, `diagnose`, `latency`, `report`, `failures`, `gen-test` subcommands |
| `.bob/` | `mcp.json.example`, `custom_modes.yaml`, and three skill files |
| `tests/` | Unit and integration tests for each layer |

**Non-goals**

- No middleware injection; no special FastAPI handling.
- No log forwarding, metrics export, or OpenTelemetry compatibility.
- No per-request files, no rotation — one append-only `traces/traces.jsonl`.
- No distributed tracing across process boundaries.

---

## Sub-Tasks

---

### Sub-Task 0 — Sandbox app (written by hand, committed undecorated)

**Intent**
Provide a realistic demo target that exists before the rest of the package is built. The sandbox bugs are intentional but **not documented in any repo file** — the agent must discover them through tracing. Committing it first gives Sub-Task 4 a real target to run `diagnose` against instead of relying on fixture JSONL alone.

**Expected Outcomes**

- `sandbox/app.py` is a working FastAPI app with at least one buggy endpoint and one slow N+1 endpoint.
- The app has zero `bobtrace` references — it is the "inherited service" state.
- `sandbox/README.md` describes the app's purpose and endpoints but says nothing about where the bugs are.
- Running `uvicorn sandbox.app:app` starts without errors.

**Todo List**

1. Write `sandbox/db.py`: an in-memory data store with helper functions (at least one of which contains a latent bug).
2. Write `sandbox/models.py`: Pydantic models for the app's domain objects.
3. Write `sandbox/app.py`: FastAPI app with at least two endpoints — one that triggers the bug, one that triggers the N+1.
4. Write `sandbox/README.md`: describes the app, its endpoints, and how to start it. No bug hints.
5. Confirm the app starts cleanly with `uvicorn sandbox.app:app --reload`.

**Relevant Context**

- The bugs must not appear in any README, comment, or docstring in the repo. This is the answer key.
- The N+1 pattern must involve a parent function calling the same child function ≥ 3 times sequentially so the detector fires.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

### Sub-Task 1 — Package skeleton and project files

**Intent**
Establish the installable package layout, dependencies, and entry points so every subsequent sub-task has a stable home.

**Expected Outcomes**

- `pyproject.toml` defines the `bobtrace` package and a `bobtrace` CLI entry point.
- Core package (`bobtrace/`) has **no third-party dependencies** — standard library only.
- `mcp` is an optional server extra; `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `pytest`, and `httpx` are demo/test extras.
- Running `pip install -e ".[server,dev]"` succeeds.
- `.bob/mcp.json.example` skeleton exists; `.bob/mcp.json` is gitignored.

**Dependency groups in `pyproject.toml`**

```
[project]                     # no dependencies
[project.optional-dependencies]
server = ["mcp"]
dev    = ["fastapi", "uvicorn", "httpx", "pytest"]
```

**Todo List**

1. Create `bobtrace/__init__.py` (version string only).
2. Create `pyproject.toml` with the dependency groups above and `[project.scripts]` entry `bobtrace = bobtrace.cli:main`.
3. Create `main.py` thin shim calling `bobtrace.cli:main`.
4. Create `tests/__init__.py` and `tests/generated/.gitkeep`.
5. Create `.bob/mcp.json.example` skeleton with interpreter path placeholder (`<venv>/Scripts/python.exe` on Windows, `<venv>/bin/python` on Unix).
6. Add `.bob/mcp.json` to `.gitignore`.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

### Sub-Task 2 — Runtime tracer (`bobtrace/tracer.py`)

**Intent**
Implement the `@bob_trace` decorator and everything needed to record spans, propagate context, and flush complete traces to JSONL — with no third-party dependencies.

**Expected Outcomes**

- `from bobtrace.tracer import bob_trace` works with stdlib only.
- A root call (nothing in `ContextVar`) creates a new `trace_id`, a new `TraceBuffer`, and becomes the root span.
- A child call inherits the buffer from the `ContextVar` and joins the same `trace_id`.
- Flush: serialise each span to a JSON string, concatenate with newlines, write the whole string in a **single** `file.write()` call per trace. One atomic write prevents concurrent processes interleaving lines.
- Error traces always written. Successful traces sampled at `BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE` (float 0–1, default `1.0`).
- Trace capped at 500 spans; root carries `dropped_spans` when hit.
- `BOBTRACE_FILE` overrides path; empty string disables output.
- Works for both sync and async functions.
- `BaseException` (not `Exception`) → `cancelled`, re-raised immediately.
- `Exception` → `error`, re-raised unchanged.
- Tracer failures are swallowed — they never affect the application.

**ContextVar value**

The `ContextVar` holds a named triple `(trace_id, current_span_id, buffer)`. `TraceBuffer` has `spans: list`, `has_error: bool`, `dropped: int`. A root call creates the buffer; children inherit it. No module-level span list.

**Raw span schema (one span per JSONL line)**

| Field | Present | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `trace_id` | always | UUID |
| `span_id` | always | UUID |
| `parent_span_id` | always | UUID or `null` |
| `function_name` | always | `__name__` |
| `module` | always | `__module__` |
| `qualname` | always | `__qualname__` |
| `source_file` | always | Absolute path (made project-relative in read path) |
| `source_line` | always | Line number of `def` |
| `start_time` | always | ISO-8601 UTC |
| `status` | always | `success`, `error`, or `cancelled` |
| `execution_time_ms` | always | Wall time |
| `inputs` | always | Serialised argument dict |
| `response` | success only | Serialised return value |
| `error_type` | error only | Exception class name |
| `error_message` | error only | `"<Type>: <str(exc)>"` — used as bug title |
| `error_location` | error only | `"file:line"` of the raise site (innermost traceback frame) |
| `dropped_spans` | root only | Only when cap hit |

**Input serialisation spec**

- Bind arguments to parameter names using signature cached at decoration time.
- JSON scalars and stdlib containers: pass through (max depth 6, max 50 items, max 2 000-char strings).
- Pydantic models: `.model_dump()` if available.
- `datetime`, `Decimal`, `UUID`, `Path`, `Enum`, `bytes`: `repr()`.
- Everything else: `__dict__` / `__slots__` plus `__type__`.
- Redact fields matching `password`, `token`, `email`, `phone`, or `BOBTRACE_REDACT_KEYS` to `"***REDACTED***"`. Redacted spans are recorded and written — they do not block test generation.
- Re-entrancy guard: if tracer serialisation calls a traced function, that inner call records nothing.

**Todo List**

1. Define `Span` dataclass with all schema fields.
2. Define `TraceBuffer` dataclass: `spans`, `has_error`, `dropped`.
3. Implement `ContextVar[Optional[Tuple[str, str, TraceBuffer]]]` with read/set helpers.
4. Implement `bob_trace` decorator factory for sync and async callables: create buffer on root entry, link parent on child entry, record span on exit, flush on root exit.
5. Implement input serialisation with depth/size limits, type dispatch, redaction, re-entrancy guard.
6. Implement flush: one `file.write()` call per trace containing all spans, each on its own line.
7. Implement sampling and 500-span cap with `dropped_spans` on the root span.
8. Write `tests/test_tracer.py`: root span, child linking, error fields, `BaseException` → cancelled, async, sampling, cap, serialisation depth/redaction/re-entrancy, single-write-per-trace assertion (mock `open`).

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

### Sub-Task 3 — AST injector/ejector (`bobtrace/injector.py`)

**Intent**
Implement the source-rewriting engine that adds and removes `@bob_trace` decorators and the matching import, fully reversibly and idempotently, with atomic file writes.

**Expected Outcomes**

- `inject_file` adds `@bob_trace` immediately above every `def`/`async def` that does not already have it, and inserts the import.
- Per-function idempotency: a function that already has `@bob_trace` is skipped; other functions in the same file are still processed.
- `eject_file` removes lines that are exactly `@bob_trace` (with matching indent) and the exact import line; resulting bytes match the pre-inject file.
- `compile()` validation before any write; if it fails, the original file is untouched.
- Atomic write via `os.replace`.
- CRLF preserved end-to-end.
- `--dry-run` prints unified diff, exits 0, writes nothing.

**Per-function skip rules**

- Already has `@bob_trace` on the line immediately above → skip silently.
- Dunder method other than `__init__` or `__call__` → skip silently.
- Body contains a call to `sys._getframe`, `inspect.currentframe`, `inspect.stack`, or same family → skip and **report** with reason.
- File's absolute path is inside the `bobtrace` package → refuse entire file.

Do NOT skip `__init__.py` or files under `tests/`.

**Import placement**

Insert `from bobtrace.tracer import bob_trace` after the module docstring and any `__future__` imports. Eject removes that exact line only. No sentinel comment. Pre-existing manual import will also be removed by eject — document this trade-off in README.

**Todo List**

1. Implement `inject_file(path, dry_run)`: use `ast` to locate `FunctionDef`/`AsyncFunctionDef` line numbers; line-level insertion (not `ast.unparse`) to preserve formatting.
2. Apply per-function skip logic (existing decorator, dunder filter, frame-inspection detection, bobtrace-package guard).
3. Implement `eject_file(path, dry_run)`: remove `@bob_trace` lines and exact import line.
4. `compile()` validation + atomic `os.replace`.
5. Detect and preserve CRLF.
6. Implement `inject` and `eject` CLI subcommands in `bobtrace/cli.py`, print summary.
7. `--dry-run` with `difflib.unified_diff`.
8. Write `tests/test_injector.py`: inject → eject = original bytes, double-inject idempotent per-function, dry-run writes nothing, dunders skipped, frame-inspection reported, CRLF round-trips, bobtrace files refused.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

### Sub-Task 4 — Analysis store (`bobtrace/store.py`) and MCP server (`bobtrace/mcp_server.py`)

**Intent**
Implement all 7 analysis functions as pure Python in `store.py`, wire exactly 7 of them as MCP tools in `mcp_server.py`. `load_traces` and `compute_self_ms` are internal helpers, not tools.

**MCP SDK compatibility**

Try `from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer` first; fall back to `from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP`. Insert project root into `sys.path[0]` at module top.

**Read-path computed fields** (never written by the tracer)

- `self_ms`: span's `execution_time_ms` minus direct children's `execution_time_ms`.
- Propagation label: error span whose direct child also errored → `"propagated <Type> from child"` in compact view.
- All file paths in agent-facing payloads are **project-relative**.

**7 MCP tools**

| Tool | CLI cmd | Key inputs | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `diagnose` | `diagnose` | _(none)_ | Docstring: "START HERE for errors" |
| `explain_latency` | `latency` | `trace_id` (optional) | Docstring: "START HERE for slowness" |
| `generate_regression_test` | `gen-test` | `span_id`, `write` (bool default `true`) | |
| `get_trace` | _(MCP only)_ | `trace_id` | Compact nested tree |
| `list_failures` | `failures` | `limit` (int default 10) | |
| `trace_summary` | `report` | _(none)_ | |
| `get_slowest` | _(MCP only)_ | `limit` (int default 10) | |

**`diagnose` / `list_failures` root-cause spec**

Distinct bug = error span with no failing child, grouped by `(function_name, error_type, error_location)`. Each group:

- `occurrences`: count
- `affected_entry_points`: distinct `function_name` of root spans containing this bug
- `location`: project-relative `source_file:error_location` (the **raise** line)
- `source_snippet`: up to 5 lines from disk centred on raise line; failing line prefixed `>> `; line numbers shown; wrapped in try/except
- `call_path`: ordered list of `{fn, inputs}` from root to error span
- `example_span_ids`: up to 3 span IDs
- `next_step`: always `"generate_regression_test(span_id='<id>')"` — no heuristic

**`explain_latency` spec**

No `trace_id`: pick root span (`parent_span_id == null`) with highest `execution_time_ms`. If none, return `{"error": "no traces recorded"}`.
With `trace_id`: analyse all spans sharing that ID.

Output:
- `self_time_by_function`: `[{fn, call_count, self_ms, share_pct}]` sorted by `self_ms` desc
- `hot_path`: greedy walk — at each node descend into child with largest `execution_time_ms`; stop at leaf; returns `[{fn, span_id, ms}]`
- `n_plus_one_suspects`: see N+1 spec
- `caveats`: trust-the-numbers warnings — `"Root span ended with status=error; timings stop at the failure"` and `"Fewer than 5 recorded requests for this entry point; confirm with more traffic"`; not span-drop counts

**N+1 detection**

Within one trace: parent suspect when same child `function_name` called ≥ 3 times AND sequential (each start ≥ previous start + execution_time_ms − 0.1 ms). Parallel calls not a suspect.
Report: `parent_fn`, `child_fn`, `call_count`, `total_ms`, `pct_of_request`, `heaviest_inner_fn`.

**`get_trace` compact node**

`fn`, `span_id`, `status`, `ms`, `self_ms`, `inputs` (show `***REDACTED***`, do not strip — a missing key reads as "argument not passed"). On success: `response`. On error: `error` (`"propagated <Type> from child"` if direct child also failed, else `error_message`), `at` (project-relative `error_location`, originating span only). Children in `calls` ordered by `start_time`.

**`generate_regression_test` spec**

- `span_id` required. Does not fall back to latest failure.
- Requires `module` and `qualname`.
- Refuse if: qualname contains `<locals>` (nested function) OR qualname contains `.` and does not end in `.__init__` or `.__call__` (method). Two distinct checks.
- Redacted inputs (`"***REDACTED***"`): generate the test; add header comment `# NOTE: replace ***REDACTED*** values with safe fixture values before running. Never paste a ***REDACTED*** marker into code or tests.`
- Filename: `tests/generated/test_replay_<qualname>_<span_id[:8]>.py` (sanitise qualname for filesystem).
- Generated test sets `os.environ["BOBTRACE_FILE"] = ""` and `os.environ["BOBTRACE_CONSOLE"] = "off"` before importing the target.
- **Error span** — test that fails while the bug still exists:
  ```python
  try:
      result = function(**inputs)
  except RecordedExceptionType:
      pytest.fail("still raises RecordedExceptionType")
  except Exception:
      raise
  else:
      pytest.fail("Bug no longer reproduces. Replace this line with an assertion on the intended result.")
  ```
- **Success span** — characterization test: `assert serialize(result) == RECORDED_RESPONSE`.
- `write=True`: write file, return `{"path": ..., "source": ...}`.
- `write=False`: return `{"filename": ..., "source": ...}`.

**`trace_summary` spec**

Per-function aggregation, errors first. Fields: `fn`, `call_count`, `error_count`, `error_rate`, `p50_ms`, `p95_ms`, `total_self_ms`. When `BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE < 1.0`, append one caveat line: `"Warning: error_rate is inflated — successful traces are sampled at <rate> while error traces are always recorded."`.

**`get_slowest` spec**

Slowest spans in file by `execution_time_ms`, each with `self_ms` and project-relative `source_file`. Default `limit=10`.

**Todo List**

1. Implement `load_traces(path)` — reads JSONL, returns flat span list and `{trace_id: [spans]}` dict.
2. Implement `compute_self_ms(spans)` — subtract direct children's `execution_time_ms` from each span.
3. Implement `diagnose(traces)`.
4. Implement `explain_latency(traces, trace_id=None)` with greedy hot_path and N+1 detection.
5. Implement `list_failures(traces, limit=10)`.
6. Implement `trace_summary(traces)` with sample-rate caveat.
7. Implement `get_slowest(traces, limit=10)`.
8. Implement `get_trace(traces, trace_id)` — compact nested tree; show `***REDACTED***`, do not strip.

# bobtrace — Plan

## Top-Level Overview

`bobtrace` is a Python package that lets a developer point at any directory of Python source files, automatically inject a `@bob_trace` decorator onto every function via AST rewriting, and then read back structured execution evidence through an MCP server that Bob (or any agent) calls to diagnose bugs, explain latency, and generate regression tests — without the developer having to add a single line of instrumentation manually.

**Scope**

| Layer | What it does |
|---|---|
| `sandbox/` | Demo FastAPI app — written by hand before any other sub-task, committed undecorated |
| `bobtrace/tracer.py` | Runtime: `@bob_trace` decorator, context propagation via `ContextVar`, span recording, JSONL flush |
| `bobtrace/injector.py` | AST-based injector/ejector: rewrites source files to add/remove the decorator and import |
| `bobtrace/store.py` | Pure analysis functions shared by the MCP server and the CLI |
| `bobtrace/mcp_server.py` | Stdio MCP server: 7 tools the agent calls |
| `bobtrace/cli.py` / `main.py` | Entry point: `inject`, `eject`, `diagnose`, `latency`, `report`, `failures`, `gen-test` subcommands |
| `.bob/` | `mcp.json.example`, `custom_modes.yaml`, and three skill files |
| `tests/` | Unit and integration tests for each layer |

**Non-goals**

- No middleware injection; no special FastAPI handling.
- No log forwarding, metrics export, or OpenTelemetry compatibility.
- No per-request files, no rotation — one append-only `traces/traces.jsonl`.
- No distributed tracing across process boundaries.

---

## Sub-Tasks

---

### Sub-Task 0 — Sandbox app (written by hand, committed undecorated)

**Intent**
Provide a realistic demo target that exists before the rest of the package is built. The sandbox bugs are intentional but **not documented in any repo file** — the agent must discover them through tracing. Committing it first gives Sub-Task 4 a real target to run `diagnose` against instead of relying on fixture JSONL alone.

**Expected Outcomes**

- `sandbox/app.py` is a working FastAPI app with at least one buggy endpoint and one slow N+1 endpoint.
- The app has zero `bobtrace` references — it is the "inherited service" state.
- `sandbox/README.md` describes the app's purpose and endpoints but says nothing about where the bugs are.
- Running `uvicorn sandbox.app:app` starts without errors.

**Todo List**

1. Write `sandbox/db.py`: an in-memory data store with helper functions (at least one of which contains a latent bug).
2. Write `sandbox/models.py`: Pydantic models for the app's domain objects.
3. Write `sandbox/app.py`: FastAPI app with at least two endpoints — one that triggers the bug, one that triggers the N+1.
4. Write `sandbox/README.md`: describes the app, its endpoints, and how to start it. No bug hints.
5. Confirm the app starts cleanly with `uvicorn sandbox.app:app --reload`.

**Relevant Context**

- The bugs must not appear in any README, comment, or docstring in the repo. This is the answer key.
- The N+1 pattern must involve a parent function calling the same child function ≥ 3 times sequentially so the detector fires.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

### Sub-Task 1 — Package skeleton and project files

**Intent**
Establish the installable package layout, dependencies, and entry points so every subsequent sub-task has a stable home.

**Expected Outcomes**

- `pyproject.toml` defines the `bobtrace` package and a `bobtrace` CLI entry point.
- Core package (`bobtrace/`) has **no third-party dependencies** — standard library only.
- `mcp` is an optional server extra; `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `pytest`, and `httpx` are demo/test extras.
- Running `pip install -e ".[server,dev]"` succeeds.
- `.bob/mcp.json.example` skeleton exists; `.bob/mcp.json` is gitignored.

**Dependency groups in `pyproject.toml`**

```
[project]                     # no dependencies
[project.optional-dependencies]
server = ["mcp"]
dev    = ["fastapi", "uvicorn", "httpx", "pytest"]
```

**Todo List**

1. Create `bobtrace/__init__.py` (version string only).
2. Create `pyproject.toml` with the dependency groups above and `[project.scripts]` entry `bobtrace = bobtrace.cli:main`.
3. Create `main.py` thin shim calling `bobtrace.cli:main`.
4. Create `tests/__init__.py` and `tests/generated/.gitkeep`.
5. Create `.bob/mcp.json.example` skeleton with interpreter path placeholder (`<venv>/Scripts/python.exe` on Windows, `<venv>/bin/python` on Unix).
6. Add `.bob/mcp.json` to `.gitignore`.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

### Sub-Task 2 — Runtime tracer (`bobtrace/tracer.py`)

**Intent**
Implement the `@bob_trace` decorator and everything needed to record spans, propagate context, and flush complete traces to JSONL — with no third-party dependencies.

**Expected Outcomes**

- `from bobtrace.tracer import bob_trace` works with stdlib only.
- A root call (nothing in `ContextVar`) creates a new `trace_id`, a new `TraceBuffer`, and becomes the root span.
- A child call inherits the buffer from the `ContextVar` and joins the same `trace_id`.
- Flush: serialise each span to a JSON string, concatenate with newlines, write the whole string in a **single** `file.write()` call per trace. One atomic write prevents concurrent processes interleaving lines.
- Error traces always written. Successful traces sampled at `BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE` (float 0–1, default `1.0`).
- Trace capped at 500 spans; root carries `dropped_spans` when hit.
- `BOBTRACE_FILE` overrides path; empty string disables output.
- Works for both sync and async functions.
- `BaseException` (not `Exception`) → `cancelled`, re-raised immediately.
- `Exception` → `error`, re-raised unchanged.
- Tracer failures are swallowed — they never affect the application.

**ContextVar value**

The `ContextVar` holds a named triple `(trace_id, current_span_id, buffer)`. `TraceBuffer` has `spans: list`, `has_error: bool`, `dropped: int`. A root call creates the buffer; children inherit it. No module-level span list.

**Raw span schema (one span per JSONL line)**

| Field | Present | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `trace_id` | always | UUID |
| `span_id` | always | UUID |
| `parent_span_id` | always | UUID or `null` |
| `function_name` | always | `__name__` |

# bobtrace — Plan

## Top-Level Overview

`bobtrace` is a Python package that lets a developer point at any directory of Python source files, automatically inject a `@bob_trace` decorator onto every function via AST rewriting, and then read back structured execution evidence through an MCP server that Bob (or any agent) calls to diagnose bugs, explain latency, and generate regression tests — without the developer having to add a single line of instrumentation manually.

**Scope**

| Layer | What it does |
|---|---|
| `bobtrace/tracer.py` | Runtime: `@bob_trace` decorator, context propagation via `ContextVar`, span recording, JSONL flush |
| `bobtrace/injector.py` | AST-based injector/ejector: rewrites source files to add/remove the decorator and import |
| `bobtrace/store.py` | Pure analysis functions shared by the MCP server and the CLI |
| `bobtrace/mcp_server.py` | Stdio MCP server: 7 tools the agent calls |
| `bobtrace/cli.py` / `main.py` | Entry point: `inject`, `eject`, `diagnose`, `latency`, `report`, `failures`, `gen-test` subcommands |
| `.bob/` | `mcp.json.example`, `custom_modes.yaml`, and three skills |
| `tests/` | Unit and integration tests for each layer |
| `sandbox/` | A small FastAPI app used for demo/integration testing — bugs are intentional and undocumented in the repo |

**Non-goals**

- No middleware injection; no special FastAPI handling.
- No log forwarding, metrics export, or OpenTelemetry compatibility.
- No per-request files, no rotation — one append-only `traces/traces.jsonl`.
- No distributed tracing across process boundaries.

### Sub-Task 2 — Runtime tracer (`bobtrace/tracer.py`)

**Intent**
Implement the `@bob_trace` decorator and everything needed to record spans, propagate context, and flush complete traces to JSONL — with no third-party dependencies.

**Expected Outcomes**

- `from bobtrace.tracer import bob_trace` works with stdlib only.
- A decorated call with nothing in the `ContextVar` creates a new `trace_id`, a new buffer, and becomes the root span.
- A decorated call that finds a buffer in the `ContextVar` joins the same `trace_id` as a child.
- The full trace is flushed as **one `write()` call per trace** (all spans, each on its own line, concatenated) when the root span finishes. One atomic write prevents concurrent processes from interleaving lines.
- Error traces are always written. Successful traces are sampled at `BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE` (float 0–1, default `1.0`).
- A single trace is capped at 500 spans; the root span carries `dropped_spans` when the cap is hit.
- `BOBTRACE_FILE` overrides the output path; an empty string disables file output.
- Works for both sync and async functions.
- `BaseException` (but not `Exception`) closes the span as `cancelled` and is re-raised immediately.
- `Exception` closes the span as `error` and is re-raised unchanged.
- Failures inside the tracer itself are swallowed so they never affect the application.

**ContextVar value structure**

The `ContextVar` holds a single value: a named triple `(trace_id, current_span_id, buffer)`. The buffer is an object with three attributes: `spans` (list), `has_error` (bool), `dropped` (int). A new root call creates the buffer; all children inherit it through the same `ContextVar` value. There is no module-level span list.

**Raw span schema (written to JSONL — one span per line)**

| Field | Always present | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `trace_id` | yes | UUID |
| `span_id` | yes | UUID |
| `parent_span_id` | yes | UUID or `null` for root |
| `function_name` | yes | Simple name (`__name__`) |
| `module` | yes | `__module__` of the function |
| `qualname` | yes | `__qualname__` |
| `source_file` | yes | Absolute path (made project-relative in the read path) |
| `source_line` | yes | Line number of the `def` |
| `start_time` | yes | ISO-8601 UTC |
| `status` | yes | `success`, `error`, or `cancelled` |
| `execution_time_ms` | yes | Wall time of this span |
| `inputs` | yes | Serialised argument dict (see serialisation spec) |
| `response` | on success | Serialised return value |
| `error_type` | on error | Exception class name |
| `error_message` | on error | `"<Type>: <str(exc)>"` — used as the bug title |
| `error_location` | on error | `"file:line"` of the raise site (innermost traceback frame) |
| `dropped_spans` | root only | Integer, only present when cap was hit |

**Input serialisation spec**

- Bind arguments to parameter names using the signature cached at decoration time (`inspect.signature`).
- Serialise without running arbitrary user code: JSON scalars and stdlib containers pass through as-is (max depth 6, max 50 items per container, max 2 000-char strings).
- `Pydantic` models: call `.model_dump()` if available.
- `datetime`, `Decimal`, `UUID`, `Path`, `Enum`, `bytes`: `repr()`.
- Everything else: `__dict__` or `__slots__` plus a `__type__` key.
- Redact fields whose name matches `password`, `token`, `email`, `phone`, or any key in `BOBTRACE_REDACT_KEYS` (comma-separated env var) to `"***REDACTED***"`. Redacted inputs are **recorded and written** — they do not prevent span recording or test generation.
- A re-entrancy guard: if the tracer's own serialisation code calls a traced function, that inner call records nothing.

**Todo List**

1. Define the `Span` dataclass with all fields listed in the schema above.
2. Define the `TraceBuffer` dataclass: `spans`, `has_error`, `dropped`.
3. Implement the `ContextVar[Optional[Tuple[str, str, TraceBuffer]]]` with helpers to read/set the current context.
4. Implement `bob_trace` as a decorator factory wrapping both sync and async callables: create buffer on root entry, link parent on child entry, record span on exit, flush on root exit.
5. Implement the input serialisation function with depth/size limits, type dispatch, redaction, and re-entrancy guard.
6. Implement the flush function: serialize each span to a JSON string, concatenate with newlines, write the whole string in a single `file.write()` call.
7. Implement sampling and the 500-span cap with `dropped_spans` on the root span.
8. Write unit tests in `tests/test_tracer.py`: root span creation, child linking, error fields, `BaseException` → `cancelled`, async support, sampling, span cap, serialisation depth/redaction/re-entrancy, single-write flush (mock `open` and assert one `write` call per trace).

**Relevant Context**

- `module` and `qualname` are needed by `generate_regression_test` to import and call the function.
- `source_file` is stored absolute by the tracer; `store.py` makes it project-relative in all agent-facing payloads.

| Tool | CLI cmd | Key inputs | Key outputs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `diagnose` | `diagnose` | _(none)_ | Root-cause groups — START HERE for errors |
| `explain_latency` | `latency` | `trace_id` (optional) | `self_time_by_function`, `hot_path`, `n_plus_one_suspects`, `caveats` — START HERE for slowness |
| `generate_regression_test` | `gen-test` | `span_id`, `write` (bool default `true`) | `path`+`source` or `filename`+`source` |
| `get_trace` | _(MCP only)_ | `trace_id` | Compact nested tree |
| `list_failures` | `failures` | `limit` (int default 10) | Root-cause groups, ≤ 3 example span IDs each |
| `trace_summary` | `report` | _(none)_ | Per-function stats, errors first |

**`diagnose` / `list_failures` root-cause spec**

A distinct bug is an error span with **no failing child** (the deepest error in the chain), grouped by `(function_name, error_type, error_location)`. Each group:

- `occurrences`: count of matching spans
- `affected_entry_points`: distinct `function_name` of root spans containing this bug
- `location`: project-relative `source_file:error_location` (the **raise** line, not the `def` line)
- `source_snippet`: up to 5 lines from disk centred on the raise line; failing line prefixed with `>> ` and line numbers shown; wrapped in try/except so missing files don't crash the tool
- `call_path`: ordered list of `{fn, inputs}` from root span to error span
- `example_span_ids`: up to 3 span IDs
- `next_step`: always `"generate_regression_test(span_id='<example_span_id>')"` — no heuristic

**`explain_latency` spec**

With no `trace_id`: scan all spans where `parent_span_id == null`, pick the one with the highest `execution_time_ms`. If none, return `{"error": "no traces recorded"}`.
With a `trace_id`: analyse all spans sharing that ID.

Output:
- `self_time_by_function`: list of `{fn, call_count, self_ms, share_pct}` sorted by `self_ms` desc
- `hot_path`: greedy walk from root — at each node descend into the child with the largest `execution_time_ms`; stop at a leaf; returns list of `{fn, span_id, ms}`
- `n_plus_one_suspects`: see N+1 spec below
- `caveats`: trust-the-numbers warnings only — e.g. `"Root span ended with status=error; timings stop at the failure"` and `"Fewer than 5 recorded requests for this entry point; confirm with more traffic"`. Not span-drop counts.

**N+1 detection spec**

Within one trace a parent is a suspect when it calls the same child `function_name` ≥ 3 times AND those calls are **sequential** (each call's `start_time ≥ previous start_time + execution_time_ms − 0.1 ms`). Parallel calls of the same child are not a suspect.

Report per suspect: `parent_fn`, `child_fn`, `call_count`, `total_ms`, `pct_of_request`, `heaviest_inner_fn` (the `function_name` with the most total `self_ms` among descendants of those calls).

**`get_trace` compact node spec**

Each node: `fn`, `span_id`, `status`, `ms` (`execution_time_ms`), `self_ms`, `inputs`. On success: `response`. On error: `error` (`"propagated <Type> from child"` if a direct child also failed, otherwise `error_message`), `at` (project-relative `error_location`, only on the originating span). Children in `calls` ordered by `start_time`.

**`generate_regression_test` spec**

- Takes `span_id` (required). Does not fall back to latest failure.
- Requires `module` and `qualname` on the span.
- Refuse with an error string if: `qualname` contains `<locals>` (nested function) OR `qualname` contains `.` and does not end in `.__init__` or `.__call__` (method). These two checks are distinct.
- Spans with redacted inputs (`"***REDACTED***"`) are **not refused**: generate the test and add a header comment `# NOTE: replace ***REDACTED*** values with safe fixture values before running`.
- Filename: `tests/generated/test_replay_<qualname>_<span_id[:8]>.py` (sanitise qualname for filesystem).
- Generated test file sets `os.environ["BOBTRACE_FILE"] = ""` and `os.environ["BOBTRACE_CONSOLE"] = "off"` before importing the target, so running the test suite does not record traces of itself.
- **Error span** → test that **fails while the bug still exists**:
  ```python
  # The test should FAIL until the bug is fixed.
  result = function(**inputs)
  # if recorded exception type is still raised → pytest.fail("still raises <Type>")
  # if a different exception is raised → re-raise it (let pytest report it)
  # if the call returns without error → pytest.fail("Bug no longer reproduces. Replace this line with an assertion on the intended result.")
  ```
- **Success span** → characterization test: `assert serialize(result) == RECORDED_RESPONSE`.
- `write=True` (default): write file, return `{"path": ..., "source": ...}`.
- `write=False`: return `{"filename": ..., "source": ...}` only.

# bobtrace — Plan

## Top-Level Overview

`bobtrace` is a Python package that lets a developer point at any directory of Python source files, automatically inject a `@bob_trace` decorator onto every function via AST rewriting, and then read back structured execution evidence through an MCP server that Bob (or any agent) calls to diagnose bugs, explain latency, and generate regression tests — without the developer having to add a single line of instrumentation manually.

**Scope**

| Layer | What it does |
|---|---|
| `sandbox/` | Demo FastAPI app — written by hand before any other sub-task, committed undecorated |
| `bobtrace/tracer.py` | Runtime: `@bob_trace` decorator, context propagation via `ContextVar`, span recording, JSONL flush |
| `bobtrace/injector.py` | AST-based injector/ejector: rewrites source files to add/remove the decorator and import |
| `bobtrace/store.py` | Pure analysis functions shared by the MCP server and the CLI |
| `bobtrace/mcp_server.py` | Stdio MCP server: 7 tools the agent calls |
| `bobtrace/cli.py` / `main.py` | Entry point: `inject`, `eject`, `diagnose`, `latency`, `report`, `failures`, `gen-test` subcommands |
| `.bob/` | `mcp.json.example`, `custom_modes.yaml`, and three skill files |
| `tests/` | Unit and integration tests for each layer |

**Non-goals**

- No middleware injection; no special FastAPI handling.
- No log forwarding, metrics export, or OpenTelemetry compatibility.
- No per-request files, no rotation — one append-only `traces/traces.jsonl`.
- No distributed tracing across process boundaries.

### Sub-Task 2 — Runtime tracer (`bobtrace/tracer.py`)

**Intent**
Implement the `@bob_trace` decorator and everything needed to record spans, propagate context, and flush complete traces to JSONL — with no third-party dependencies.

**Expected Outcomes**

- `from bobtrace.tracer import bob_trace` works with stdlib only.
- A root call (nothing in `ContextVar`) creates a new `trace_id`, a new `TraceBuffer`, and becomes the root span.
- A child call inherits the buffer from the `ContextVar` and joins the same `trace_id`.
- Flush: serialise each span to a JSON string, concatenate with newlines, write the whole string in a **single** `file.write()` call per trace. One atomic write prevents concurrent processes interleaving lines.
- Error traces always written. Successful traces sampled at `BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE` (float 0–1, default `1.0`).
- Trace capped at 500 spans; root carries `dropped_spans` when hit.
- `BOBTRACE_FILE` overrides path; empty string disables output.
- Works for both sync and async functions.
- `BaseException` (not `Exception`) → `cancelled`, re-raised immediately.
- `Exception` → `error`, re-raised unchanged.
- Tracer failures are swallowed — they never affect the application.

**ContextVar value**

The `ContextVar` holds a named triple `(trace_id, current_span_id, buffer)`. `TraceBuffer` has `spans: list`, `has_error: bool`, `dropped: int`. A root call creates the buffer; children inherit it. No module-level span list.

**Raw span schema (one span per JSONL line)**

| Field | Present | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `trace_id` | always | UUID |
| `span_id` | always | UUID |
| `parent_span_id` | always | UUID or `null` |
| `function_name` | always | `__name__` |
| `module` | always | `__module__` |
| `qualname` | always | `__qualname__` |
| `source_file` | always | Absolute path (made project-relative in read path) |
| `source_line` | always | Line number of `def` |
| `start_time` | always | ISO-8601 UTC |
| `status` | always | `success`, `error`, or `cancelled` |
| `execution_time_ms` | always | Wall time |
| `inputs` | always | Serialised argument dict |
| `response` | success only | Serialised return value |
| `error_type` | error only | Exception class name |
| `error_message` | error only | `"<Type>: <str(exc)>"` — used as bug title |
| `error_location` | error only | `"file:line"` of the raise site (innermost traceback frame) |
| `dropped_spans` | root only | Only when cap hit |

**Input serialisation spec**

- Bind arguments to parameter names using signature cached at decoration time.
- JSON scalars and stdlib containers: pass through (max depth 6, max 50 items, max 2 000-char strings).
- Pydantic models: `.model_dump()` if available.
- `datetime`, `Decimal`, `UUID`, `Path`, `Enum`, `bytes`: `repr()`.
- Everything else: `__dict__` / `__slots__` plus `__type__`.
- Redact fields matching `password`, `token`, `email`, `phone`, or `BOBTRACE_REDACT_KEYS` to `"***REDACTED***"`. Redacted spans are recorded and written — they do not block test generation.
- Re-entrancy guard: if tracer serialisation calls a traced function, that inner call records nothing.

**`diagnose` / `list_failures` root-cause spec**

Distinct bug = error span with no failing child, grouped by `(function_name, error_type, error_location)`. Each group:

- `occurrences`: count
- `affected_entry_points`: distinct `function_name` of root spans containing this bug
- `location`: project-relative `source_file:error_location` (the **raise** line)
- `source_snippet`: up to 5 lines from disk centred on raise line; failing line prefixed `>> `; line numbers shown; wrapped in try/except
- `call_path`: ordered list of `{fn, inputs}` from root to error span
- `example_span_ids`: up to 3 span IDs
- `next_step`: always `"generate_regression_test(span_id='<id>')"` — no heuristic

**`explain_latency` spec**

No `trace_id`: pick root span (`parent_span_id == null`) with highest `execution_time_ms`. If none, return `{"error": "no traces recorded"}`.
With `trace_id`: analyse all spans sharing that ID.

Output:
- `self_time_by_function`: `[{fn, call_count, self_ms, share_pct}]` sorted by `self_ms` desc
- `hot_path`: greedy walk — at each node descend into child with largest `execution_time_ms`; stop at leaf; returns `[{fn, span_id, ms}]`
- `n_plus_one_suspects`: see N+1 spec
- `caveats`: trust-the-numbers warnings — `"Root span ended with status=error; timings stop at the failure"` and `"Fewer than 5 recorded requests for this entry point; confirm with more traffic"`; not span-drop counts

**N+1 detection**

Within one trace: parent suspect when same child `function_name` called ≥ 3 times AND sequential (each start ≥ previous start + execution_time_ms − 0.1 ms). Parallel calls not a suspect.
Report: `parent_fn`, `child_fn`, `call_count`, `total_ms`, `pct_of_request`, `heaviest_inner_fn`.

**`get_trace` compact node**

`fn`, `span_id`, `status`, `ms`, `self_ms`, `inputs` (show `***REDACTED***`, do not strip — a missing key reads as "argument not passed"). On success: `response`. On error: `error` (`"propagated <Type> from child"` if direct child also failed, else `error_message`), `at` (project-relative `error_location`, originating span only). Children in `calls` ordered by `start_time`.

**`generate_regression_test` spec**

- `span_id` required. Does not fall back to latest failure.
- Requires `module` and `qualname`.
- Refuse if: qualname contains `<locals>` (nested function) OR qualname contains `.` and does not end in `.__init__` or `.__call__` (method). Two distinct checks.
- Redacted inputs (`"***REDACTED***"`): generate the test; add header comment `# NOTE: replace ***REDACTED*** values with safe fixture values before running. Never paste a ***REDACTED*** marker into code or tests.`
- Filename: `tests/generated/test_replay_<qualname>_<span_id[:8]>.py` (sanitise qualname for filesystem).
- Generated test sets `os.environ["BOBTRACE_FILE"] = ""` and `os.environ["BOBTRACE_CONSOLE"] = "off"` before importing the target.
- **Error span** — test that fails while the bug still exists:
  ```python
  try:
      result = function(**inputs)
  except RecordedExceptionType:
      pytest.fail("still raises RecordedExceptionType")
  except Exception:
      raise
  else:
      pytest.fail("Bug no longer reproduces. Replace this line with an assertion on the intended result.")
  ```
- **Success span** — characterization test: `assert serialize(result) == RECORDED_RESPONSE`.
- `write=True`: write file, return `{"path": ..., "source": ...}`.
- `write=False`: return `{"filename": ..., "source": ...}`.

**`trace_summary` spec**

Per-function aggregation, errors first. Fields: `fn`, `call_count`, `error_count`, `error_rate`, `p50_ms`, `p95_ms`, `total_self_ms`. When `BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE < 1.0`, append one caveat line: `"Warning: error_rate is inflated — successful traces are sampled at <rate> while error traces are always recorded."`.

**`get_slowest` spec**

Slowest spans in file by `execution_time_ms`, each with `self_ms` and project-relative `source_file`. Default `limit=10`.

---

### What changed in this revision

**Breaking behavior fixes:**
- **Flush**: each span is its own line; all lines concatenated into one `file.write()` per trace — no concurrent interleaving
- **ContextVar**: value is a `(trace_id, span_id, buffer)` triple; `TraceBuffer` is the only span accumulator; no module-level list

# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
