**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'

Contents of file bobtrace-plan.md:

1 | # bobtrace — Plan
2 | 
3 | ## Top-Level Overview
4 | 
5 | `bobtrace` is a Python package that lets a developer point at any directory of Python source files, automatically inject a `@bob_trace` decorator onto every function via AST rewriting, and then read back structured execution evidence through an MCP server that Bob (or any agent) calls to diagnose bugs, explain latency, and generate regression tests — without the developer having to add a single line of instrumentation manually.
6 | 
7 | **Scope**
8 | 
9 | | Layer | What it does |
10 | |---|---|
11 | | `sandbox/` | Demo FastAPI app — written by hand before any other sub-task, committed undecorated |
12 | | `bobtrace/tracer.py` | Runtime: `@bob_trace` decorator, context propagation via `ContextVar`, span recording, JSONL flush |
13 | | `bobtrace/injector.py` | AST-based injector/ejector: rewrites source files to add/remove the decorator and import |
14 | | `bobtrace/store.py` | Pure analysis functions shared by the MCP server and the CLI |
15 | | `bobtrace/mcp_server.py` | Stdio MCP server: 7 tools the agent calls |
16 | | `bobtrace/cli.py` / `main.py` | Entry point: `inject`, `eject`, `diagnose`, `latency`, `report`, `failures`, `gen-test` subcommands |
17 | | `.bob/` | `mcp.json.example`, `custom_modes.yaml`, and three skill files |
18 | | `tests/` | Unit and integration tests for each layer |
19 | 
20 | **Non-goals**
21 | 
22 | - No middleware injection; no special FastAPI handling.
23 | - No log forwarding, metrics export, or OpenTelemetry compatibility.
24 | - No per-request files, no rotation — one append-only `traces/traces.jsonl`.
25 | - No distributed tracing across process boundaries.
26 |

The sandbox bugs are intentional but **not documented in any repo file** — the agent must discover them through tracing. Committing it first gives Sub-Task 4 a real target to run `diagnose` against instead of relying on fixture JSONL alone.

97 | ### Sub-Task 2 — Runtime tracer (`bobtrace/tracer.py`)
98 | 
99 | **Intent**
100 | Implement the `@bob_trace` decorator and everything needed to record spans, propagate context, and flush complete traces to JSONL — with no third-party dependencies.
101 | 
102 | **Expected Outcomes**
103 | 
104 | - `from bobtrace.tracer import bob_trace` works with stdlib only.
105 | - A root call (nothing in `ContextVar`) creates a new `trace_id`, a new `TraceBuffer`, and becomes the root span.
106 | - A child call inherits the buffer from the `ContextVar` and joins the same `trace_id`.
107 | - Flush: serialise each span to a JSON string, concatenate with newlines, write the whole string in a **single** `file.write()` call per trace. One atomic write prevents concurrent processes interleaving lines.
108 | - Error traces always written. Successful traces sampled at `BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE` (float 0–1, default `1.0`).
109 | - Trace capped at 500 spans; root carries `dropped_spans` when hit.
110 | - `BOBTRACE_FILE` overrides path; empty string disables output.
111 | - Works for both sync and async functions.
112 | - `BaseException` (not `Exception`) → `cancelled`, re-raised immediately.
113 | - `Exception` → `error`, re-raised unchanged.
114 | - Tracer failures are swallowed — they never affect the application.
115 | 
116 | **ContextVar value**
117 | 
118 | The `ContextVar` holds a named triple `(trace_id, current_span_id, buffer)`. `TraceBuffer` has `spans: list`, `has_error: bool`, `dropped: int`. A root call creates the buffer; children inherit it. No module-level span list.
119 | 
120 | **Raw span schema (one span per JSONL line)**
121 | 
122 | | Field | Present | Notes |
123 | |---|---|---|
124 | | `trace_id` | always | UUID |
125 | | `span_id` | always | UUID |
126 | | `parent_span_id` | always | UUID or `null` |
127 | | `function_name` | always | `__name__` |
128 | | `module` | always | `__module__` |
129 | | `qualname` | always | `__qualname__` |
130 | | `source_file` | always | Absolute path (made project-relative in read path) |
131 | | `source_line` | always | Line number of `def` |
132 | | `start_time` | always | ISO-8601 UTC |
133 | | `status` | always | `success`, `error`, or `cancelled` |
134 | | `execution_time_ms` | always | Wall time |
135 | | `inputs` | always | Serialised argument dict |
136 | | `response` | success only | Serialised return value |
137 | | `error_type` | error only | Exception class name |
138 | | `error_message` | error only | `"<Type>: <str(exc)>"` — used as bug title |
139 | | `error_location` | error only | `"file:line"` of the raise site (innermost traceback frame) |
140 | | `dropped_spans` | root only | Only when cap hit |
141 | 
142 | **Input serialisation spec**
143 | 
144 | - Bind arguments to parameter names using signature cached at decoration time.
145 | - JSON scalars and stdlib containers: pass through (max depth 6, max 50 items, max 2 000-char strings).
146 | - Pydantic models: `.model_dump()` if available.
147 | - `datetime`, `Decimal`, `UUID`, `Path`, `Enum`, `bytes`: `repr()`.
148 | - Everything else: `__dict__` / `__slots__` plus `__type__`.
149 | - Redact fields matching `password`, `token`, `email`, `phone`, or `BOBTRACE_REDACT_KEYS` to `"***REDACTED***"`. Redacted spans are recorded and written — they do not block test generation.
150 | - Re-entrancy guard: if tracer serialisation calls a traced function, that inner call records nothing.
151 | 
152 | **Todo List**
153 | 
154 | 1. Define `Span` dataclass with all schema fields.
155 | 2. Define `TraceBuffer` dataclass: `spans`, `has_error`, `dropped`.
156 | 3. Implement `ContextVar[Optional[Tuple[str, str, TraceBuffer]]]` with read/set helpers.
157 | 4. Implement `bob_trace` decorator factory for sync and async callables: create buffer on root entry, link parent on child entry, record span on exit, flush on root exit.
158 | 5. Implement input serialisation with depth/size limits, type dispatch, redaction, re-entrancy guard.
159 | 6. Implement flush: one `file.write()` call per trace containing all spans, each on its own line.
160 | 7. Implement sampling and 500-span cap with `dropped_spans` on the root span.
161 | 8. Write `tests/test_tracer.py`: root span, child linking, error fields, `BaseException` → cancelled, async, sampling, cap, serialisation depth/redaction/re-entrancy, single-write-per-trace assertion (mock `open`).
162 | 
163 | **Status** `[ ] pending`

167 | ### Sub-Task 3 — AST injector/ejector (`bobtrace/injector.py`)
168 | 
169 | **Intent**
170 | Implement the source-rewriting engine that adds and removes `@bob_trace` decorators and the matching import, fully reversibly and idempotently, with atomic file writes.
171 | 
172 | **Expected Outcomes**
173 | 
174 | - `inject_file` adds `@bob_trace` immediately above every `def`/`async def` that does not already have it, and inserts the import.
175 | - Per-function idempotency: a function that already has `@bob_trace` is skipped; other functions in the same file are still processed.
176 | - `eject_file` removes lines that are exactly `@bob_trace` (with matching indent) and the exact import line; resulting bytes match the pre-inject file.
177 | - `compile()` validation before any write; if it fails, the original file is untouched.
178 | - Atomic write via `os.replace`.
179 | - CRLF preserved end-to-end.
180 | - `--dry-run` prints unified diff, exits 0, writes nothing.
181 | 
182 | **Per-function skip rules**
183 | 
184 | - Already has `@bob_trace` on the line immediately above → skip silently.
185 | - Dunder method other than `__init__` or `__call__` → skip silently.
186 | - Body contains a call to `sys._getframe`, `inspect.currentframe`, `inspect.stack`, or same family → skip and **report** with reason.
187 | - File's absolute path is inside the `bobtrace` package → refuse entire file.
188 | 
189 | Do NOT skip `__init__.py` or files under `tests/`.
190 | 
191 | **Import placement**
192 | 
193 | Insert `from bobtrace.tracer import bob_trace` after the module docstring and any `__future__` imports. Eject removes that exact line only. No sentinel comment. Pre-existing manual import will also be removed by eject — document this trade-off in README.
194 | 
195 | **Todo List**
196 | 
197 | 1. Implement `inject_file(path, dry_run)`: use `ast` to locate `FunctionDef`/`AsyncFunctionDef` line numbers; line-level insertion (not `ast.unparse`) to preserve formatting.
198 | 2. Apply per-function skip logic (existing decorator, dunder filter, frame-inspection detection, bobtrace-package guard).
199 | 3. Implement `eject_file(path, dry_run)`: remove `@bob_trace` lines and exact import line.
200 | 4. `compile()` validation + atomic `os.replace`.
201 | 5. Detect and preserve CRLF.
202 | 6. Implement `inject` and `eject` CLI subcommands in `bobtrace/cli.py`, print summary.
203 | 7. `--dry-run` with `difflib.unified_diff`.
204 | 8. Write `tests/test_injector.py`: inject → eject = original bytes, double-inject idempotent per-function, dry-run writes nothing, dunders skipped, frame-inspection reported, CRLF round-trips, bobtrace files refused.

210 | ### Sub-Task 4 — Analysis store (`bobtrace/store.py`) and MCP server (`bobtrace/mcp_server.py`)
211 | 
212 | **Intent**
213 | Implement all 7 analysis functions as pure Python in `store.py`, wire exactly 7 of them as MCP tools in `mcp_server.py`. `load_traces` and `compute_self_ms` are internal helpers, not tools.
214 | 
215 | **MCP SDK compatibility**
216 | 
217 | Try `from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer` first; fall back to `from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP`. Insert project root into `sys.path[0]` at module top.
218 | 
219 | **Read-path computed fields** (never written by the tracer)
220 | 
221 | - `self_ms`: span's `execution_time_ms` minus direct children's `execution_time_ms`.
222 | - Propagation label: error span whose direct child also errored → `"propagated <Type> from child"` in compact view.
223 | - All file paths in agent-facing payloads are **project-relative**.
224 | 
225 | **7 MCP tools**
226 | 
227 | | Tool | CLI cmd | Key inputs | Notes |
228 | |---|---|---|---|
229 | | `diagnose` | `diagnose` | _(none)_ | Docstring: "START HERE for errors" |
230 | | `explain_latency` | `latency` | `trace_id` (optional) | Docstring: "START HERE for slowness" |
231 | | `generate_regression_test` | `gen-test` | `span_id`, `write` (bool default `true`) | |
232 | | `get_trace` | _(MCP only)_ | `trace_id` | Compact nested tree |
233 | | `list_failures` | `failures` | `limit` (int default 10) | |
234 | | `trace_summary` | `report` | _(none)_ | |
235 | | `get_slowest` | _(MCP only)_ | `limit` (int default 10) | |
236 | 
237 | **`diagnose` / `list_failures` root-cause spec**
238 | 
239 | Distinct bug = error span with no failing child, grouped by `(function_name, error_type, error_location)`. Each group:
240 | 
241 | - `occurrences`: count
242 | - `affected_entry_points`: distinct `function_name` of root spans containing this bug
243 | - `location`: project-relative `source_file:error_location` (the **raise** line)
244 | - `source_snippet`: up to 5 lines from disk centred on raise line; failing line prefixed `>> `; line numbers shown; wrapped in try/except
245 | - `call_path`: ordered list of `{fn, inputs}` from root to error span
246 | - `example_span_ids`: up to 3 span IDs
247 | - `next_step`: always `"generate_regression_test(span_id='<id>')"` — no heuristic
248 | 
249 | **`explain_latency` spec**
250 | 
251 | No `trace_id`: pick root span (`parent_span_id == null`) with highest `execution_time_ms`. If none, return `{"error": "no traces recorded"}`.
252 | With `trace_id`: analyse all spans sharing that ID.
253 | 
254 | Output:
255 | - `self_time_by_function`: `[{fn, call_count, self_ms, share_pct}]` sorted by `self_ms` desc
256 | - `hot_path`: greedy walk — at each node descend into child with largest `execution_time_ms`; stop at leaf; returns `[{fn, span_id, ms}]`
257 | - `n_plus_one_suspects`: see N+1 spec
258 | - `caveats`: trust-the-numbers warnings — `"Root span ended with status=error; timings stop at the failure"` and `"Fewer than 5 recorded requests for this entry point; confirm with more traffic"`; not span-drop counts
259 | 
260 | **N+1 detection**
261 | 
262 | Within one trace: parent suspect when same child `function_name` called ≥ 3 times AND sequential (each start ≥ previous start + execution_time_ms − 0.1 ms). Parallel calls not a suspect.
263 | Report: `parent_fn`, `child_fn`, `call_count`, `total_ms`, `pct_of_request`, `heaviest_inner_fn`.
264 | 
265 | **`get_trace` compact node**
266 | 
267 | `fn`, `span_id`, `status`, `ms`, `self_ms`, `inputs` (show `***REDACTED***`, do not strip — a missing key reads as "argument not passed"). On success: `response`. On error: `error` (`"propagated <Type> from child"` if direct child also failed, else `error_message`), `at` (project-relative `error_location`, originating span only). Children in `calls` ordered by `start_time`.
268 | 
269 | **`generate_regression_test` spec**
270 | 
271 | - `span_id` required. Does not fall back to latest failure.
272 | - Requires `module` and `qualname`.
273 | - Refuse if: qualname contains `<locals>` (nested function) OR qualname contains `.` and does not end in `.__init__` or `.__call__` (method). Two distinct checks.
274 | - Redacted inputs (`"***REDACTED***"`): generate the test; add header comment `# NOTE: replace ***REDACTED*** values with safe fixture values before running. Never paste a ***REDACTED*** marker into code or tests.`
275 | - Filename: `tests/generated/test_replay_<qualname>_<span_id[:8]>.py` (sanitise qualname for filesystem).
276 | - Generated test sets `os.environ["BOBTRACE_FILE"] = ""` and `os.environ["BOBTRACE_CONSOLE"] = "off"` before importing the target.
277 | - **Error span** — test that fails while the bug still exists:
278 |   ```python
279 |   try:
280 |       result = function(**inputs)
281 |   except RecordedExceptionType:
282 |       pytest.fail("still raises RecordedExceptionType")
283 |   except Exception:
284 |       raise
285 |   else:
286 |       pytest.fail("Bug no longer reproduces. Replace this line with an assertion on the intended result.")
287 |   ```
288 | - **Success span** — characterization test: `assert serialize(result) == RECORDED_RESPONSE`.
289 | - `write=True`: write file, return `{"path": ..., "source": ...}`.
290 | - `write=False`: return `{"filename": ..., "source": ...}`.
291 | 
292 | **`trace_summary` spec**
293 | 
294 | Per-function aggregation, errors first. Fields: `fn`, `call_count`, `error_count`, `error_rate`, `p50_ms`, `p95_ms`, `total_self_ms`. When `BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE < 1.0`, append one caveat line: `"Warning: error_rate is inflated — successful traces are sampled at <rate> while error traces are always recorded."`.
295 | 
296 | **`get_slowest` spec**
297 | 
298 | Slowest spans in file by `execution_time_ms`, each with `self_ms` and project-relative `source_file`. Default `limit=10`.

+import copy
+from typing import Dict, List, Optional
+
+_orders: Dict[int, dict] = {
+    1: {"id": 1, "user_id": 1, "item_ids": [10, 11], "status": "shipped"},
+    2: {"id": 2, "user_id": 2, "item_ids": [12], "status": "pending"},
+    3: {"id": 3, "user_id": 1, "item_ids": [10, 13, 14], "status": "delivered"},
+    4: {"id": 4, "user_id": 3, "item_ids": [11], "status": "pending"},
+    5: {"id": 5, "user_id": 2, "item_ids": [13, 14], "status": "cancelled"},
+}
+
+_items: Dict[int, dict] = {
+    10: {"id": 10, "name": "Widget A", "price": 9.99},
+    11: {"id": 11, "name": "Widget B", "price": 14.99},
+    12: {"id": 12, "name": "Gadget X", "price": 49.99},
+    13: {"id": 13, "name": "Gadget Y", "price": 29.99},
+    14: {"id": 14, "name": "Doohickey", "price": 4.99},
+}
+
+_users: Dict[int, dict] = {
+    1: {"id": 1, "name": "Alice", "email": "alice@example.com"},
+    2: {"id": 2, "name": "Bob", "email": "bob@example.com"},
+    3: {"id": 3, "name": "Carol", "email": "carol@example.com"},
+}
+
+_discount_codes: Dict[str, float] = {
+    "SAVE10": 0.10,
+    "HALF":   0.50,
+    "VIP":    0.20,
+}
+
+
+def get_order(order_id: int) -> Optional[dict]:
+    row = _orders.get(order_id)
+    if row is None:
+        return None
+    return copy.copy(row)
+
+
+def get_item(item_id: int) -> Optional[dict]:
+    row = _items.get(item_id)
+    if row is None:
+        return None
+    return copy.copy(row)
+
+
+def get_user(user_id: int) -> Optional[dict]:
+    row = _users.get(user_id)
+    if row is None:
+        return None
+    return copy.copy(row)
+
+
+def list_orders(user_id: Optional[int] = None) -> List[dict]:
+    rows = list(_orders.values())
+    if user_id is not None:
+        rows = [r for r in rows if r["user_id"] == user_id]
+    return [copy.copy(r) for r in rows]
+
+
+def apply_discount(price: float, code: str) -> float:
+    rate = _discount_codes.get(code.upper())
+    if rate is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unknown discount code: {code!r}")
+    return round(price - (price * rate), 2)
+
+
+def compute_order_total(order_id: int, discount_code: Optional[str] = None) -> float:
+    order = get_order(order_id)
+    if order is None:
+        raise KeyError(f"Order {order_id} not found")
+
+    total = 0.0
+    for item_id in order["item_ids"]:
+        item = get_item(item_id)
+        if item is not None:
+            total += item["price"]
+
+    if discount_code:
+        total = apply_discount(total, discount_code)
+
+    return round(total, 2)
+
+
+def get_order_summary(order_id: int) -> dict:
+    order = get_order(order_id)
+    if order is None:
+        raise KeyError(f"Order {order_id} not found")
+    user = get_user(order["user_id"])
+    items = [get_item(iid) for iid in order["item_ids"]]
+    subtotal = sum(i["price"] for i in items if i)
+    return {
+        "order_id": order_id,
+        "user": user,
+        "items": items,
+        "subtotal": round(subtotal, 2),
+        "status": order["status"],
+    }

Actually, cleaner: the bug is that `apply_discount` in `db.py` does `price - (price * rate)` but when called with `price=0.0` it silently returns 0 instead of raising — not interesting enough.

Actually the cleanest approach: the `discount_code` lookup is case-sensitive in the wrong direction. The bug is: when `code` has a trailing space (e.g. `"SAVE10 "`), `code.upper()` still doesn't strip it, so the dict lookup silently fails and raises `ValueError("Unknown discount code: 'SAVE10 '")`. The endpoint doesn't strip the input.

Even cleaner: put the bug in one clear place — `compute_order_total` returns the raw subtotal and ignores the discount when the order total is zero (no items). arguments.content:
# Order Service

A small demo service for managing orders, users, and items. It uses an in-memory data store so no database setup is required.

## Starting the service

```bash
uvicorn sandbox.app:app --reload
```

The service will be available at `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.

Interactive API docs are at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/items/{item_id}` | Retrieve a single item by ID |
| `GET` | `/users/{user_id}` | Retrieve a user by ID |
| `GET` | `/orders/{order_id}` | Retrieve an order by ID |
| `GET` | `/orders/{order_id}/total` | Calculate the total for an order, with optional discount code (`?code=SAVE10`) |
| `GET` | `/users/{user_id}/orders` | List all orders for a user, each with full item details |

## Seed data

The in-memory store is pre-loaded with:

- **Users** — IDs 1 (Alice), 2 (Bob), 3 (Carol)
- **Items** — IDs 10–14 (Widget A/B, Gadget X/Y, Doohickey)
- **Orders** — IDs 1–6 across all three users

## Discount codes

Pass `?code=<CODE>` to `/orders/{order_id}/total` to apply a discount:

| Code | Discount |
|------|----------|
| `SAVE10` | 10 % |
| `HALF` | 50 % |
| `VIP` | 20 % |

## Requirements

```
fastapi
uvicorn
pydantic
```

Install with:

```bash
pip install fastapi uvicorn
```

+from typing import Optional
+
+from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Query
+
+from sandbox import db
+from sandbox.models import (
+    Item,
+    Order,
+    OrderSummary,
+    OrderTotal,
+    User,
+    UserOrdersResponse,
+)
+
+app = FastAPI(title="Order Service")
+
+
+@app.get("/items/{item_id}", response_model=Item)
+def read_item(item_id: int):
+    row = db.get_item(item_id)
+    if row is None:
+        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
+    return row
+
+
+@app.get("/users/{user_id}", response_model=User)
+def read_user(user_id: int):
+    row = db.get_user(user_id)
+    if row is None:
+        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="User not found")
+    return row
+
+
+@app.get("/orders/{order_id}", response_model=Order)
+def read_order(order_id: int):
+    row = db.get_order(order_id)
+    if row is None:
+        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Order not found")
+    return row
+
+
+@app.get("/orders/{order_id}/total", response_model=OrderTotal)
+def get_order_total(
+    order_id: int,
+    code: Optional[str] = Query(default=None),
+):
+    total = db.compute_order_total(order_id, code)
+    return OrderTotal(order_id=order_id, total=total, discount_code=code)
+
+
+@app.get("/users/{user_id}/orders", response_model=UserOrdersResponse)
+def get_user_orders(user_id: int):
+    user_row = db.get_user(user_id)
+    if user_row is None:
+        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="User not found")
+
+    orders = db.list_orders(user_id=user_id)
+    summaries = []
+    for order in orders:
+        summary = db.get_order_summary(order["id"])
+        summaries.append(summary)
+
+    return UserOrdersResponse(user=user_row, orders=summaries)

# Order Service

A small demo service for managing orders, users, and items. It uses an in-memory data store so no database setup is required.

## Starting the service

```bash
uvicorn sandbox.app:app --reload
```

The service will be available at `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.

Interactive API docs are at `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`.

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/items/{item_id}` | Retrieve a single item by ID |
| `GET` | `/users/{user_id}` | Retrieve a user by ID |
| `GET` | `/orders/{order_id}` | Retrieve an order by ID |
| `GET` | `/orders/{order_id}/total` | Calculate the total for an order, with optional discount code (`?code=SAVE10`) |
| `GET` | `/users/{user_id}/orders` | List all orders for a user, each with full item details |

## Seed data

The in-memory store is pre-loaded with:

- **Users** — IDs 1 (Alice), 2 (Bob), 3 (Carol)
- **Items** — IDs 10–14 (Widget A/B, Gadget X/Y, Doohickey)
- **Orders** — IDs 1–6 across all three users

## Discount codes

Pass `?code=<CODE>` to `/orders/{order_id}/total` to apply a discount:

| Code | Discount |
|------|----------|
| `SAVE10` | 10 % |
| `HALF` | 50 % |
| `VIP` | 20 % |

## Requirements

```
fastapi
uvicorn
pydantic
```

Install with:

```bash
pip install fastapi uvicorn
```

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# Mode Switching

You can switch between different modes using the switch_mode tool. Each mode provides access to different capabilities and tools optimized for specific types of tasks.

**When to switch modes:**
- The user explicitly requests a mode switch
- You need a tool that is ONLY available in another mode and is absolutely required to complete the task

**DO NOT switch modes when:**
- You can accomplish the task with your current tools
- The request is ambiguous

Stay in your current mode unless there is an explicit, compelling reason to switch. When in doubt, do not switch.

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

For factual questions that require knowledge about IBM products, platforms, languages, commands, APIs, configuration, documented behavior, compatibility, or product-specific errors, consult IBM documentation before answering.
This includes technologies such as IBM i, IBM Z, z/OS, Db2, CICS, COBOL, JCL, RPG, AIX, and watsonx, even when the user does not explicitly say IBM.

# Subagents
You have access to `spawn_subagent` which creates an independent agent with its own context.

**Default: do the work yourself.** Most tasks are faster and cheaper without a subagent.
Only consider a subagent when ALL of these apply:
- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back
- It would add significant irrelevant content to your context
- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

Available types:
- "explore": Explore codebase (read tools, explorer model)
- "general": Inherits current mode tools, default model

**fork_context**: Set to true when the subagent needs to understand prior conversation — e.g., decisions made, constraints discovered, or user preferences expressed earlier.
Leave false (default) when the description alone is sufficient context.

Do NOT use subagents for:
- Simple file reads, searches, or single-tool operations
- Tasks where you already have relevant context
- Quick lookups that would take fewer turns done directly

# create_chart — chart output
Use the `create_chart` tool when the user asks for a chart or data visualisation.

## How it works
Call the tool with:
- `type`: one of LineChart | BarChart | PieChart | ScatterChart | RadarChart | BoxplotChart
- `title`: short human-readable title for the chart tile
- `props`: a JSON string of chart-specific props

The props JSON must be valid for the chosen chart type. Do NOT wrap it in a spec fence.
Example for BarChart:
{"xAxisData":["Jan","Feb","Mar"],"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[4200,5800,3900]}],"title":"Monthly Revenue"}

Activate the `create-chart` skill before building props to get the full per-type prop schemas.

176 | - `eject_file` removes lines that are exactly `@bob_trace` (with matching indent) and the exact import line; resulting bytes match the pre-inject file.
177 | - `compile()` validation before any write; if it fails, the original file is untouched.
178 | - Atomic write via `os.replace`.
179 | - CRLF preserved end-to-end.
180 | - `--dry-run` prints unified diff, exits 0, writes nothing.
181 | 
182 | **Per-function skip rules**
183 | 
184 | - Already has `@bob_trace` on the line immediately above → skip silently.
185 | - Dunder method other than `__init__` or `__call__` → skip silently.
186 | - Body contains a call to `sys._getframe`, `inspect.currentframe`, `inspect.stack`, or same family → skip and **report** with reason.
187 | - File's absolute path is inside the `bobtrace` package → refuse entire file.
188 | 
189 | Do NOT skip `__init__.py` or files under `tests/`.
190 | 
191 | **Import placement**
192 | 
193 | Insert `from bobtrace.tracer import bob_trace` after the module docstring and any `__future__` imports. Eject removes that exact line only. No sentinel comment. Pre-existing manual import will also be removed by eject — document this trade-off in README.

227 | | Tool | CLI cmd | Key inputs | Notes |

229 | | `diagnose` | `diagnose` | _(none)_ | Docstring: "START HERE for errors" |
230 | | `explain_latency` | `latency` | `trace_id` (optional) | Docstring: "START HERE for slowness" |

237 | **`diagnose` / `list_failures` root-cause spec**
238 | 
239 | Distinct bug = error span with no failing child, grouped by `(function_name, error_type, error_location)`. Each group:
240 | 
241 | - `occurrences`: count
242 | - `affected_entry_points`: distinct `function_name` of root spans containing this bug
243 | - `location`: project-relative `source_file:error_location` (the **raise** line)
244 | - `source_snippet`: up to 5 lines from disk centred on raise line; failing line prefixed `>> `; line numbers shown; wrapped in try/except

246 | - `example_span_ids`: up to 3 span IDs

250 | 
251 | No `trace_id`: pick root span (`parent_span_id == null`) with highest `execution_time_ms`. If none, return `{"error": "no traces recorded"}`.

255 | - `self_time_by_function`: `[{fn, call_count, self_ms, share_pct}]` sorted by `self_ms` desc

258 | - `caveats`: trust-the-numbers warnings — `"Root span ended with status=error; timings stop at the failure"` and `"Fewer than 5 recorded requests for this entry point; confirm with more traffic"`; not span-drop counts
259 |

261 | 
262 | Within one trace: parent suspect when same child `function_name` called ≥ 3 times AND sequential (each start ≥ previous start + execution_time_ms − 0.1 ms). Parallel calls not a suspect.
263 | Report: `parent_fn`, `child_fn`, `call_count`, `total_ms`, `pct_of_request`, `heaviest_inner_fn`.

On error: `error` (`"propagated <Type> from child"` if direct child also failed, else `error_message`), `at` (project-relative `error_location`, originating span only). Children in `calls` ordered by `start_time`.

271 | - `span_id` required. Does not fall back to latest failure.

274 | - Redacted inputs (`"***REDACTED***"`): generate the test; add header comment `# NOTE: replace ***REDACTED*** values with safe fixture values before running. Never paste a ***REDACTED*** marker into code or tests.`

276 | - Generated test sets `os.environ["BOBTRACE_FILE"] = ""` and `os.environ["BOBTRACE_CONSOLE"] = "off"` before importing the target.
277 | - **Error span** — test that fails while the bug still exists:

Read bobtrace-plan.md for full context. You are implementing Sub-Task 2: the runtime tracer (bobtrace/tracer.py).

Key requirements (read the plan for full detail):

1. ContextVar holds a triple (trace_id, current_span_id, buffer). TraceBuffer is a dataclass with spans: list, has_error: bool, dropped: int. No module-level span list.

2. Raw span schema — one span per JSONL line (see plan for all fields). source_file is absolute (store.py makes it project-relative later). error_message is "<Type>: <str(exc)>".

3. Input serialisation (cached signature at decoration time):
   - JSON scalars + stdlib containers: depth 6, max 50 items, max 2000-char strings
   - Pydantic: .model_dump()
   - datetime/Decimal/UUID/Path/Enum/bytes: repr()
   - Everything else: __dict__ or __slots__ + __type__
   - Redact password/token/email/phone + BOBTRACE_REDACT_KEYS to "***REDACTED***"
   - Re-entrancy guard: if tracer serialisation calls a traced function, that inner call records nothing
   - Redacted spans are still written — they never block test generation

4. Flush: serialise each span to JSON, join with newlines, ONE file.write() call per trace (prevents concurrent interleaving)

5. BaseException (not Exception) → status=cancelled, re-raised immediately
   Exception → status=error, re-raised unchanged
   Tracer failures swallowed

6. Sampling: BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE (float 0-1, default 1.0). Error traces always written.
7. 500-span cap: root gets dropped_spans field when hit.
8. BOBTRACE_FILE overrides path; empty string disables output.
9. Works for both sync and async functions.

Write bobtrace/tracer.py and tests/test_tracer.py.

Tests must cover: root span creation, child linking, error fields (error_type, error_message, error_location), BaseException→cancelled, async support, sampling, cap, serialisation depth/redaction/re-entrancy, single-write-per-trace (mock open, assert one write() call per trace).

Run pytest tests/test_tracer.py and make it pass.

data.content:
Sub-Task 2 is complete. Implemented bobtrace/tracer.py and tests/test_tracer.py; all 39 tests pass with no warnings.

Key implementation details:
- **bobtrace/tracer.py** (stdlib-only):
  - `Span` dataclass with all schema fields; `to_dict()` omits `response` on error/cancelled, omits error fields on success, only includes `dropped_spans` on root when cap is hit
  - `TraceBuffer` dataclass: `spans: list`, `has_error: bool`, `dropped: int`
  - Two `ContextVar`s: `_ctx` (holds `(trace_id, current_span_id, buffer)` triple) and `_serialising` (re-entrancy guard)
  - `bob_trace` decorator handles both sync and async functions (uses `inspect.iscoroutinefunction`, not the deprecated `asyncio` version)
  - Root detection: `_ctx.get() is None` → creates new `TraceBuffer` and `trace_id`; children inherit from context
  - 500-span cap: spans beyond cap are counted in `buffer.dropped` and their calls pass through unrecorded; root span gets `dropped_spans` field
  - Flush: single `file.write()` per trace — all spans joined with newlines, one atomic append
  - Sampling: `BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE` (0–1); error traces always written; `BOBTRACE_FILE=""` disables output entirely
  - `BaseException` (non-`Exception`) → `status=cancelled`; `Exception` → `status=error`; tracer failures swallowed
  - Input serialisation: cached signature at decoration time; depth 6, max 50 items, 2000-char string limit; Pydantic `.model_dump()`; `datetime/Decimal/UUID/Path/bytes/Enum` → `repr()`; generic objects → `__dict__`/`__slots__` + `__type__`; redacts `password/token/email/phone` + `BOBTRACE_REDACT_KEYS`; re-entrancy guard prevents recursive recording during serialisation
- **tests/test_tracer.py**: 39 test cases covering all required scenarios

This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# Mode Switching

You can switch between different modes using the switch_mode tool. Each mode provides access to different capabilities and tools optimized for specific types of tasks.

**When to switch modes:**
- The user explicitly requests a mode switch
- You need a tool that is ONLY available in another mode and is absolutely required to complete the task

**DO NOT switch modes when:**
- You can accomplish the task with your current tools
- The request is ambiguous

Stay in your current mode unless there is an explicit, compelling reason to switch. When in doubt, do not switch.

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

For factual questions that require knowledge about IBM products, platforms, languages, commands, APIs, configuration, documented behavior, compatibility, or product-specific errors, consult IBM documentation before answering.
This includes technologies such as IBM i, IBM Z, z/OS, Db2, CICS, COBOL, JCL, RPG, AIX, and watsonx, even when the user does not explicitly say IBM.
For Bob(or IBM Bob) product questions, call `search_ibm_docs` directly with `library_name: "bob"`.
For other IBM products, first call `list_ibm_doc_libraries`, select the most relevant exact library name from its response, and then call `search_ibm_docs`. Do not invent or modify library names.
You may reuse a library name already returned in the current conversation for follow-up questions about the same product.
Base factual product claims on the retrieved documentation. If no suitable library or relevant documentation is found, say so rather than guessing.
Documentation lookup is unnecessary when the request is purely about code in the workspace and does not require IBM product knowledge.

# Subagents
You have access to `spawn_subagent` which creates an independent agent with its own context.

**Default: do the work yourself.** Most tasks are faster and cheaper without a subagent.
Only consider a subagent when ALL of these apply:
- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back
- It would add significant irrelevant content to your context
- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

Available types:
- "explore": Explore codebase (read tools, explorer model)
- "general": Inherits current mode tools, default model

**fork_context**: Set to true when the subagent needs to understand prior conversation — e.g., decisions made, constraints discovered, or user preferences expressed earlier.
Leave false (default) when the description alone is sufficient context.

Do NOT use subagents for:
- Simple file reads, searches, or single-tool operations
- Tasks where you already have relevant context
- Quick lookups that would take fewer turns done directly

# create_chart — chart output
Use the `create_chart` tool when the user asks for a chart or data visualisation.

## How it works
Call the tool with:
- `type`: one of LineChart | BarChart | PieChart | ScatterChart | RadarChart | BoxplotChart
- `title`: short human-readable title for the chart tile
- `props`: a JSON string of chart-specific props

The props JSON must be valid for the chosen chart type. Do NOT wrap it in a spec fence.
Example for BarChart:
{"xAxisData":["Jan","Feb","Mar"],"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[4200,5800,3900]}],"title":"Monthly Revenue"}

Activate the `create-chart` skill before building props to get the full per-type prop schemas.

+"""

+
+Standard library only; no third-party dependencies.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import functools
+import inspect
+import json
+import os
+import traceback
+import uuid
+from contextvars import ContextVar
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from decimal import Decimal
+from enum import Enum
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Constants / env
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_SPAN_CAP = 500
+
+_BUILTIN_REDACT = {"password", "token", "email", "phone"}
+
+_SENTINEL_REDACTED = "***REDACTED***"
+
+
+def _redact_keys() -> set:
+    extra = os.environ.get("BOBTRACE_REDACT_KEYS", "")
+    return _BUILTIN_REDACT | {k.strip().lower() for k in extra.split(",") if k.strip()}
+
+
+def _sample_rate() -> float:
+    try:
+        return float(os.environ.get("BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE", "1.0"))
+    except ValueError:
+        return 1.0
+
+
+def _trace_file() -> Optional[str]:
+    """Return the target JSONL path, or None if output is disabled."""
+    v = os.environ.get("BOBTRACE_FILE", None)
+    if v is not None:
+        return v if v != "" else None  # empty string → disabled
+    return os.path.join("traces", "traces.jsonl")
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Data structures
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Span:
+    trace_id: str
+    span_id: str
+    parent_span_id: Optional[str]
+    function_name: str
+    module: str
+    qualname: str
+    source_file: str
+    source_line: int
+    start_time: str
+    status: str = "success"
+    execution_time_ms: float = 0.0
+    inputs: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    response: Any = None
+    error_type: Optional[str] = None
+    error_message: Optional[str] = None
+    error_location: Optional[str] = None
+    dropped_spans: Optional[int] = None  # root only, when cap hit
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
+        d: dict = {
+            "trace_id": self.trace_id,
+            "span_id": self.span_id,
+            "parent_span_id": self.parent_span_id,
+            "function_name": self.function_name,
+            "module": self.module,
+            "qualname": self.qualname,
+            "source_file": self.source_file,
+            "source_line": self.source_line,
+            "start_time": self.start_time,
+            "status": self.status,
+            "execution_time_ms": self.execution_time_ms,
+            "inputs": self.inputs,
+        }
+        if self.status == "success":
+            d["response"] = self.response
+        if self.status in ("error", "cancelled"):
+            if self.error_type is not None:
+                d["error_type"] = self.error_type
+            if self.error_message is not None:
+                d["error_message"] = self.error_message
+            if self.error_location is not None:
+                d["error_location"] = self.error_location
+        if self.dropped_spans is not None:
+            d["dropped_spans"] = self.dropped_spans
+        return d
+
+
+@dataclass
+class TraceBuffer:
+    spans: List[Span] = field(default_factory=list)
+    has_error: bool = False
+    dropped: int = 0
+

+_TraceTriple = Tuple[str, str, TraceBuffer]
+_ctx: ContextVar[Optional[_TraceTriple]] = ContextVar("_bobtrace_ctx", default=None)

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Input serialisation
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _serialize_value(v: Any, depth: int, redact: set) -> Any:
+    """Recursively serialize *v* with depth/size limits and redaction."""
+    if depth <= 0:
+        return repr(v)
+
+    # JSON scalars
+    if v is None or isinstance(v, (bool, int, float, str)):
+        if isinstance(v, str) and len(v) > 2000:
+            return v[:2000] + "...<truncated>"
+        return v
+
+    # Pydantic v2 / v1
+    if hasattr(v, "model_dump"):
+        return _serialize_value(v.model_dump(), depth - 1, redact)
+    if hasattr(v, "dict") and callable(v.dict):
+        try:
+            return _serialize_value(v.dict(), depth - 1, redact)
+        except Exception:
+            pass
+
+    # Special stdlib types → repr
+    if isinstance(v, (datetime, Decimal, uuid.UUID, Path, bytes, Enum)):
+        return repr(v)
+
+    # dict
+    if isinstance(v, dict):
+        items = list(v.items())[:50]
+        return {

+            for k, val in items

+    if isinstance(v, dict):  # unreachable — kept for clarity
+        pass
+
+    # list / tuple / set / frozenset
+    if isinstance(v, (list, tuple, set, frozenset)):
+        items = list(v)[:50]
+        serialized = [_serialize_value(i, depth - 1, redact) for i in items]
+        return serialized

+    # Generic object: __dict__ or __slots__
+    obj_dict: Optional[dict] = None
+    if hasattr(v, "__dict__"):
+        obj_dict = dict(v.__dict__)
+    elif hasattr(v, "__slots__"):

+"""
+bobtrace/tracer.py — @bob_trace decorator, context propagation, JSONL flush.
+
+Standard library only; no third-party dependencies.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import functools
+import inspect
+import json
+import os
+import traceback
+import uuid
+from contextvars import ContextVar
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from decimal import Decimal
+from enum import Enum
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Constants / env
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+_SPAN_CAP = 500
+
+_BUILTIN_REDACT = {"password", "token", "email", "phone"}
+
+_SENTINEL_REDACTED = "***REDACTED***"
+
+
+def _redact_keys() -> set:
+    extra = os.environ.get("BOBTRACE_REDACT_KEYS", "")
+    return _BUILTIN_REDACT | {k.strip().lower() for k in extra.split(",") if k.strip()}
+
+
+def _sample_rate() -> float:
+    try:
+        return float(os.environ.get("BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE", "1.0"))
+    except ValueError:
+        return 1.0
+
+
+def _trace_file() -> Optional[str]:
+    """Return the target JSONL path, or None if output is disabled."""
+    v = os.environ.get("BOBTRACE_FILE", None)

+# 500-span cap
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+

+        monkeypatch.setenv("BOBTRACE_FILE", str(tmp_path / "traces.jsonl"))
+
+        @bob_trace
+        def leaf():
+            return 1
+
+        @bob_trace
+        def root_fn():
+            for _ in range(600):
+                leaf()
+
+        root_fn()
+
+        lines = (tmp_path / "traces.jsonl").read_text().strip().splitlines()
+        spans = [json.loads(l) for l in lines]
+
+        # Total spans must be capped at 500

+

+class TestSerialisationDepth:
+    def test_depth_limit_truncates(self):
+        # Build a deeply nested dict
+        deep = {}
+        cur = deep
+        for i in range(10):
+            cur["nested"] = {}
+            cur = cur["nested"]
+        cur["value"] = "leaf"
+
+        from bobtrace.tracer import _redact_keys
+        result = _serialize_value(deep, 6, _redact_keys())
+
+        def count_depth(d, d_count=0):
+            if isinstance(d, dict) and d:
+                return count_depth(next(iter(d.values())), d_count + 1)
+            return d_count
+
+        # depth should not exceed 7 levels (6 recurse steps + repr at 0)
+        assert count_depth(result) <= 7
+
+    def test_list_capped_at_50(self):
+        from bobtrace.tracer import _redact_keys

+    def test_string_truncated_at_2000(self):

+        long_str = "x" * 3000
+        result = _serialize_value(long_str, 6, _redact_keys())
+        assert len(result) <= 2015  # 2000 + "...<truncated>"
+        assert "<truncated>" in result

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Serialisation: type dispatch
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+class TestSerialisationTypes:
+    def test_datetime_repr(self):

+        dt = datetime(2024, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)

+class TestRedaction:
+    def test_password_redacted_in_inputs(self, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+        monkeypatch.setenv("BOBTRACE_FILE", str(tmp_path / "traces.jsonl"))
+
+        @bob_trace
+        def login(username, password):
+            return "ok"
+
+        login("alice", "s3cr3t")
+
+        span = json.loads((tmp_path / "traces.jsonl").read_text().strip())
+        assert span["inputs"]["password"] == "***REDACTED***"
+        assert span["inputs"]["username"] == "alice"
+
+    def test_token_redacted(self, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+        monkeypatch.setenv("BOBTRACE_FILE", str(tmp_path / "traces.jsonl"))
+
+        @bob_trace
+        def call_api(token, data):
+            return data
+
+        call_api("my-secret-token", "payload")
+        span = json.loads((tmp_path / "traces.jsonl").read_text().strip())
+        assert span["inputs"]["token"] == "***REDACTED***"

+    def test_email_redacted(self, tmp_path, monkeypatch):

+        assert span["inputs"]["password"] == "***REDACTED***"

+    def test_nested_dict_key_redacted(self, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+        monkeypatch.setenv("BOBTRACE_FILE", str(tmp_path / "traces.jsonl"))

+        @bob_trace
+        def fn(payload):
+            return "ok"
+
+        fn({"password": "secret", "name": "alice"})
+        span = json.loads((tmp_path / "traces.jsonl").read_text().strip())
+        payload = span["inputs"]["payload"]
+        assert payload["password"] == "***REDACTED***"
+        assert payload["name"] == "alice"

+# Re-entrancy guard
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+class TestReentrancy:
+    def test_serialisation_reentrance_skips_recording(self, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+        """A traced function called during serialisation must not record a span."""
+        monkeypatch.setenv("BOBTRACE_FILE", str(tmp_path / "traces.jsonl"))
+
+        call_count = {"n": 0}
+
+        @bob_trace
+        def inner():
+            call_count["n"] += 1
+            return "inner"
+
+        class Tricky:
+            def __repr__(self):
+                # This calls a traced function during serialisation of inputs
+                return inner()
+
+        @bob_trace
+        def outer(x):
+            return "outer"
+
+        outer(Tricky())
+
+        lines = (tmp_path / "traces.jsonl").read_text().strip().splitlines()
+        spans = [json.loads(l) for l in lines]
+        fn_names = [s["function_name"] for s in spans]
+
+        # inner was called from __repr__ during serialisation but must NOT produce a span
+        assert "inner" not in fn_names
+        assert "outer" in fn_names
+

+# Single write() per trace
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+class TestSingleWrite:
+    def test_one_write_call_per_trace(self, monkeypatch):
+        """Flush must call file.write() exactly once per trace."""
+        monkeypatch.setenv("BOBTRACE_FILE", "traces/traces.jsonl")
+        monkeypatch.setenv("BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE", "1.0")
+
+        mock_fh = MagicMock()
+        mock_fh.__enter__ = lambda s: mock_fh
+        mock_fh.__exit__ = MagicMock(return_value=False)
+
+        with patch("builtins.open", return_value=mock_fh), \
+             patch("os.makedirs"):
+
+            @bob_trace
+            def child():
+                return "c"
+
+            @bob_trace
+            def root():
+                child()
+                child()
+                return "r"
+
+            root()
+
+        # Exactly one write() call for the entire trace (3 spans)
+        assert mock_fh.write.call_count == 1
+
+        # The single write contains all 3 spans (root + 2 children)
+        written_content = mock_fh.write.call_args[0][0]
+        lines = [l for l in written_content.strip().splitlines() if l]
+        assert len(lines) == 3

+    def test_two_independent_traces_two_writes(self, monkeypatch):

+        monkeypatch.setenv("BOBTRACE_FILE", "traces/traces.jsonl")
+        monkeypatch.setenv("BOBTRACE_SAMPLE_RATE", "1.0")
+
+        mock_fh = MagicMock()
+        mock_fh.__enter__ = lambda s: mock_fh
+        mock_fh.__exit__ = MagicMock(return_value=False)
+
+        with patch("builtins.open", return_value=mock_fh), \
+             patch("os.makedirs"):
+
+            @bob_trace
+            def standalone():
+                return "x"
+
+            standalone()
+            standalone()
+
+        assert mock_fh.write.call_count == 2
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# No response field on error spans
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+class TestSpanSchema:

+        monkeypatch.setenv("BOBTRACE_FILE", str(tmp_path / "traces.jsonl"))
+

+

+            fail()
+
+        span = json.loads((tmp_path / "traces.jsonl").read_text().strip())
+        assert "response" not in span
+
+    def test_no_error_fields_on_success_span(self, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+        monkeypatch.setenv("BOBTRACE_FILE", str(tmp_path / "traces.jsonl"))
+
+        @bob_trace

+            return 1
+

+        assert "error_type" not in span
+        assert "error_message" not in span
+        assert "error_location" not in span

Read bobtrace-plan.md for full context. You are implementing Sub-Task 3: the AST injector/ejector (bobtrace/injector.py) and the inject/eject CLI subcommands.

Key requirements:

1. inject_file(path, dry_run):
   - Use ast module to find FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef line numbers
   - Line-level text insertion (NOT ast.unparse) to preserve formatting and comments
   - Add @bob_trace immediately above def/async def — INSIDE any existing decorators (e.g. @app.get stays above, @bob_trace goes between @app.get and def)
   - Add import line after module docstring and any __future__ imports
   - Per-function idempotency: skip functions that already have @bob_trace immediately above them; other functions in same file still processed

2. Per-function skip rules:
   - Already has @bob_trace on line immediately above → skip silently
   - Dunder method other than __init__ or __call__ → skip silently
   - Body contains call to sys._getframe, inspect.currentframe, inspect.stack, or same family → skip AND report with reason
   - File's absolute path is inside the bobtrace package → refuse entire file

   Do NOT skip __init__.py or files under tests/

3. eject_file(path, dry_run):
   - Remove lines that are exactly @bob_trace (with matching indent)
   - Remove the exact import line
   - Result bytes must match pre-inject bytes exactly

4. Both operations:
   - compile() the result before writing; if fails, leave original untouched
   - Atomic write via os.replace (write to temp, then replace)
   - Detect and preserve CRLF line endings

5. CLI subcommands in bobtrace/cli.py: inject and eject subcommands that walk target directory, call per-file function, print summary ("Injected N functions across M files" / "Ejected decorators from M files")

6. --dry-run: print unified diff via difflib.unified_diff, exit 0, write nothing

Write bobtrace/injector.py, update bobtrace/cli.py with inject/eject subcommands, and write tests/test_injector.py.

Tests must cover: inject → eject produces original bytes, double-inject idempotent per-function, dry-run writes nothing, dunders skipped except __init__/__call__, frame-inspection functions reported, CRLF round-trips, bobtrace files refused.

Run pytest tests/test_injector.py and make it pass.

Sub-Task 3 is complete. All 18 tests pass.

**Files created/modified:**

1. **`bobtrace/injector.py`** — Full AST injector/ejector implementation:
   - `inject_file(path, dry_run)`: uses `ast` to locate `FunctionDef`/`AsyncFunctionDef` line numbers; performs line-level text insertion (no `ast.unparse`) to preserve formatting; places `@bob_trace` immediately above the `def` line (inside/below any existing decorators); inserts import after module docstring and `__future__` imports; atomic write via `os.replace` with `compile()` validation; CRLF detection and preservation; `--dry-run` unified diff via `difflib.unified_diff`.
   - `eject_file(path, dry_run)`: removes `@bob_trace` lines and the exact import line; byte-exact round-trip with the pre-inject file.
   - Per-function skip rules: already has `@bob_trace` above → skip silently; dunder except `__init__`/`__call__` → skip silently; `sys._getframe`/`inspect.currentframe`/`inspect.stack` etc. → skip + report; bobtrace package file → raise `ValueError`.
   - `_atomic_write`: writes to a sibling temp file, validates with `compile()`, then `os.replace`.

2. **`bobtrace/cli.py`** — New file with `inject` and `eject` subcommands using `argparse`; walks target directory; prints summary ("Injected N function(s) across M file(s)" / "Ejected decorators from M file(s)"); respects `--dry-run`.

3. **`tests/test_injector.py`** — 18 tests covering: inject→eject roundtrip, class with dunders, double-inject idempotency, partial idempotency, dry-run writes nothing, dunder filtering, `__init__`/`__call__` not skipped, `sys._getframe`/`inspect.currentframe`/`inspect.stack` reported, CRLF roundtrip, CRLF preservation, bobtrace package refused, import placement after docstring and `__future__`, `@bob_trace` inside existing decorators, exact import removal.

**One injector bug found and fixed during implementation:** the original code placed `@bob_trace` before the topmost existing decorator. Fixed to always insert immediately above the `def` line (inside any existing decorators). One test assertion for the decorator ordering was also corrected to find the `@bob_trace` between `@route` and `def hello` rather than finding the first one in the file.

# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).
